Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Twenty-year Mexican silver operator, guidance met since 2023, Gatos deal good; offset by the Jerritt Canyon failure, the SAT tax fight and a CEO who sells while promoting.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Keith Neumeyer (President & CEO, founder, since 2002 (CEO since Nov 2001 per circular)): Also Chair of First Mining Gold (TSX: FF) since 2015. Co-founder/first president of First Quantum Minerals in 1996 (unverified detail, widely reported). Vocal silver-price promoter. · Neil Beaumont (CFO, since Jul 2026): Replaced David Soares. · Steve Holmes (COO, since unverified): Runs Mexican operations; not verified this round.
Track record
  • Built First Majestic from a shell into a 3-4 mine Mexican silver producer over 20+ years; main hit is longevity and the Gatos dealsource
  • Jerritt Canyon (Nevada) bought Mar 2021 for ~US$470M in stock; mining suspended Mar 2023 for costs; restart now targeted H2 2027 — a capital-allocation miss (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/first-majestic-buys-jerritt-canyon-from-sprott-2021-03-12 ; https://www.mining.com/first-majestic-stock-plunges-as-it-shuts-down-jerritt-canyon-mine-to-reduce-costs/)
  • Gatos Silver (70% of Los Gatos) acquired Jan 2025 for ~US$970M stock; mine performing, 2026 guidance raised 5% mid-pointsource
  • Primero/San Dimas acquisition (2018) brought a Mexican SAT transfer-pricing dispute; NAFTA/ICSID arbitration filed 2021, still listed as pending (https://www.firstmajestic.com/investors/news-releases/first-majestic-provides-sat-tax-dispute-update ; https://www.iareporter.com/arbitration-cases/first-majestic-silver-v-mexico/)
  • First Mining Gold (Neumeyer chair since 2015) has not built a mine; Springpole still at permitting (unverified status)
  • 2026 guidance raised twice in two years: silver 13.0-14.4 -> 14.6-15.5 Moz, but AISC also raised 4%source

Boards today: Neumeyer: CEO First Majestic + Chair First Mining Gold = 2 public roles (circular 2026).

Fit to this job
Same job: Mexican underground silver-gold operator for 20+ years, same region, same method. New for them: Nevada refractory gold (Jerritt Canyon) was a failure and is still not restarted; Los Gatos is their first JV-operated asset with a partner (Dowa 30%).
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Neumeyer holds 4.73M shares (~0.95%, ~CA$120M) plus 0.7M options, 0.38M RSUs, 0.30M PSUs (circular Apr 2026); shares mostly from grants/options over 20 years, recent pattern is option exercise then sale (net seller ~CA$14M over 12 months to Aug 2026). CEO total comp 2025 ~US$7.43M (17% salary). Say-on-pay 2025 'strong' (percentage not extracted). Sources: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1308648/000119312526191171/d102132dex9931.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-ag/first-majestic-silver-shares/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Jerritt Canyon: ~US$470M acquisition idled after 2 years; capital-allocation miss not acknowledged as such
  • CEO net seller of stock in 2025-26 while promoting silver
  • Long-running Mexican tax dispute (SAT/ICSID) unresolved
  • CEO pay US$7.4M (2025) at the high end for a ~US$5-10B producer; 83% variable

Thesis

Four mines: Fekola (Mali, ~47% of 2026 output; open pit in a Phase-8 strip, underground stoping since Jul 2025, Fekola Regional permit finally granted Aug 7, 2026 after an 18-month slip), Goose (Nunavut; first gold Jun 2025; a crushing-circuit fire in April 2026 cut Q2 to 12,890 oz at US$6,390 AISC; mobile crusher running >3,000 tpd since mid-August, fixed-plant upgrade mid-October, 4,000 tpd design not before H2 2027), Masbate (Philippines; 180–200 koz, AISC US$1,430–1,580, the reliable one) and Otjikoto (Namibia; open pit finished, underground and stockpiles, 80–100 koz until Antelope in 2029). 2025: 979,604 oz at AISC US$1,584; 2026 guidance cut in August to 820–920 koz at AISC US$2,370–2,550 (guidance modelled at US$5,000 gold, which inflates price-linked royalties). H1 2026: 441 koz, revenue US$1.95B, adjusted net income US$301M, free cash flow US$104M after the last gold-prepay deliveries (done June) and collar losses (end December). Balance sheet: cash US$287M, US$800M revolver (US$95M drawn post-quarter), US$460M 2.75% converts due 2030 convertible at US$3.17 — deep in the money, ~145M shares of dilution; Fingold sold to Agnico for US$325M cash in April. Returns: US$0.02 quarterly dividend (~1.5%) and a buyback that took 35M shares for US$172M in H1. Reserves 8.99 Moz (Goose 2.38 Moz at 6.79 g/t; Gramalote FS Jul 2025: US$740M capex, NPV5% US$941M at US$2,500 — deferred). Founder-CEO Clive Johnson retired in June; CFO Mike Cinnamond is CEO, Kelvin Dushnisky (ex-AngloGold, ex-Barrick) executive chair. Thirteen analysts, consensus Buy, average target US$6.45.

The Gate

Whether Goose becomes the 300 koz/yr mine that justifies C$1.54B — and whether Mali lets Fekola pay for the wait. Goose has missed every number attached to it: 2025 guidance 120–150k → 80–110k → 53k delivered; 2026 '~250k' → 170–230k → 170–200k; capex C$1.25B → C$1.54B; then the fire. Steady state is now guided for H2 2027, with a ten-week fixed-plant shutdown in H1 2027 for the Phase-2 crusher, on a site fed by one winter ice road and one sealift window.

Sub-gates
  1. Mali — a junta at war with JNIM (fuel blockade since Sep 2025; the Defence Minister killed in April 2026 attacks), a 2023 code that takes 35% and 30% CIT on all new ground, and a permit that arrived 18 months late; Barrick's US$430M settlement is the precedent for how disputes end.
  2. Cost — consolidated AISC has gone US$1,584 → US$1,964 → US$2,356 in three prints and the guide is US$2,370–2,550; some is price-linked royalties, more is Fekola stripping and Goose remediation; at US$3,000 gold the margin is thin.
  3. The converts — US$460M convertible at US$3.17 means ~145M shares arrive whatever the buyback does.
  4. Namibia and the Philippines — Otjikoto has 90 koz of reserves and a hole until Antelope (2029); Masbate has 7–8 years at 0.72 g/t.
  5. A new CEO and CFO in their first year running two remediation programmes.

The market is not paying 3.5× because it missed something. It is paying 3.5× because it has watched Goose for two years.

Valuation Anchor

~3.5× EBITDA, ~US$800 per reserve ounce, 0.8–0.9× a spot NAV — the widest peer discount of any producer here, wider than Fresnillo's, and for reasons that are operational rather than structural. That is the case: Fresnillo's discount cannot close because the float cannot change; B2Gold's can, because Goose can work. If Goose reaches 4,000 tpd in H2 2027 and Fekola Regional adds 150 koz from 2028, this is a ~1.1 Moz producer with AISC back under US$2,000, and 5× EBITDA on that is roughly 2× today's price before any help from gold. The collars expire in December, so 2027 is the first fully-spot year.

The bear case is that 2027 looks like 2026: Goose stuck at 3,200 tpd through the shutdown, Fekola in a strip, AISC US$2,400, and a Mali headline — in which case 3.5× is fair, the converts arrive, and the stock is dead money at a 1.5% yield.

Bucket: producer / cash flow, the turnaround end of it — a re-rate that depends on one Arctic crusher and one Sahelian government.

Read: A widely held, founder-less senior where the only alignment signal is the company's own buyback — and where the insiders who could sell into the August rally did. Van Eck's weight makes this a GDX flow stock as much as a Mali stock. Nothing here says the people closest to Goose expect a re-rate soon; nothing says they expect disaster either.

Jurisdiction risk

Mali is the layer that prices the stock. Fekola Complex is ~47% of 2026 ounces. The Sep 2024 framework keeps the Fekola mine under the 2012 code to 2040 (80/20 with a priority dividend to the state, effective tax ~40%) and puts all regional ground under the 2023 code (65/35, 30% CIT); disputes since 2016 settled, fuel-tax exemptions surrendered. Since then: JNIM's fuel blockade from Sep 2025, national rationing in Jan 2026, coordinated attacks in April 2026 that killed the Defence Minister, a new mining ministry, and a permit that was 'Q1 2026', then 'June', then Aug 7. B2Gold says 2026 fuel is secured and ~36% hedged, 3,300 staff are 98% Malian, and processes are now 'harmonised'. Barrick's Loulo-Gounkoto settlement (US$430M, Nov 2025) is the template for what a dispute costs. Nunavut is the opposite problem — a supportive jurisdiction with brutal logistics: one winter ice road from the marine laydown, one sealift, ten-week shutdown windows, a knowledge-sharing pact with Agnico. Philippines (Masbate) and Namibia (Otjikoto, 90%) are stable and small. Colombia (Gramalote) is resettlement and an EIA modification away from a decision the company keeps deferring. Local: no material community dispute reported at any of the four mines in 2025–26; the Goose fire was an accident, not a licence event.

A four-country portfolio where one country carries half the ounces and all of the discount.

Differentiator
  1. The cheapest senior gold multiple on the market with a real path to fixing the reason: Goose is a 6.8 g/t reserve with 3.8 Moz Indicated and a district (Llama, Nuvuyak, Tattuk, George) that keeps growing — the mine is right; the crusher was wrong.
  2. Fekola Regional is permitted — the 18-month wait is over, tolling has started, and the complex can run ~500 koz/yr into the late 2030s.
  3. Capital returns while repairing — US$224M to shareholders in H1 (buyback + dividend), Fingold monetised for US$325M cash, gold prepay and collars rolling off by December.
  4. Gramalote is optional growth on the shelf — a feasibility-stage 227 koz/yr mine at US$985 AISC that nobody is paying for.
  5. A board built for the fix — Dushnisky (ran AngloGold and Barrick's operations) as executive chair over a first-year CEO.

Read it honestly: every differentiator is a repair of a self-inflicted problem. The upside is real because the execution was bad; that cuts both ways.

Exploration upside

Back River is the one that matters · moves the needle: high for Goose life, low for the multiple. US$46M and >35,000 m in 2026 (27,500 m done by August): Llama 21.2 m @ 19.1 g/t and 4.7 m @ 44.6; new Tattuk zone 150 m down-plunge of Nuvuyak, 10 m @ 10.9 g/t; George 9.4 m @ 26.5. Goose reserves are only 2.38 Moz against 3.79 Moz Indicated and 2.28 Inferred — conversion is the lever. Mali exploration is US$5M (Dandoko exploitation application 2027 for 2028). Otjikoto US$14M underground on Wolfshag/Antelope.

If Goose is a 300 koz mine for fifteen years, Back River drilling is what proves it. Watch the Dec 2026 reserve update.

Next Catalyst

Mid-Oct 2026: Goose Phase-1 crusher complete (3,200 tpd); Q3 results ~early Nov (Goose ~43 koz, Fekola Regional pre-strip, revolver balance); Dec: collars expire, first Regional ounces possible, R&R update (Goose additions, Antelope); Jan/Feb 2027: 2027 guidance — management says 'every chance' 2027 > 2026, earlier talk of ~980 koz; H1 2027: Goose Phase 2 to 4,000 tpd with a ten-week shutdown; Gramalote EIA and resettlement; Dandoko application; NCIB pace; Mali.

Open Questions
  • What does Goose actually produce in Q3 and Q4 2026 — and does the Phase-2 shutdown in H1 2027 come with enough stockpile to avoid a third missed year?
  • What is consolidated AISC at US$3,500 gold once price-linked royalties normalise — is US$2,000 reachable in 2027?
  • What is the real cost of Mali: fuel, security, the 35% state share on Regional, and repatriation — and what did the 2024 settlement cost in cash?
  • Buyback or converts: US$172M repurchased in H1 against ~145M shares coming at US$3.17 — what is the net share count in 2030?
  • When does Gramalote get a decision, and is it a build or a sale?
  • What changes under Cinnamond and Dushnisky — capital allocation, guidance discipline, Mali posture?

Aside

Guidance is modelled at US$5,000/oz gold, which is why the AISC guide (US$2,370–2,550) looks worse than the Q2 print: royalties and Mali's priority dividend scale with price. At US$3,500 the same plan is cheaper. The other way to read it: management has stopped guiding conservatively on price.

Mike Cinnamond (President & CEO, since Jun 4, 2026): CFO 2014-2026, joined 2013; accountant/finance background, first CEO role. Boards: Onyx Gold, Contango Silver & Gold. · Clive Johnson (Chair Emeritus (retired CEO), since founder 2007; retired Jun 2026): Founded Bema Gold (sold to Kinross 2007, ~US$3B — unverified) and B2Gold; built Otjikoto, Fekola, Goose. · Kelvin Dushnisky (Executive Chair, since Feb 23, 2026 (chair earlier)): Ex-Barrick president, ex-AngloGold Ashanti CEO (left 2020). · Michael McDonald (CFO, since Jun 4, 2026): Succeeded Cinnamond.
Track record
  • Johnson's record: Bema Gold built and sold to Kinross (2007); B2Gold built Otjikoto (2014) and Fekola (2017) on time and budget — wins in two cycles (unverified amounts)
  • Goose (Nunavut): bought via Sabina (Apr 2023, ~C$1.1B); capex guided ~C$800M (Sep 2023) -> C$1.05B (Jan 2024, +30%) -> C$1.54B (Sep 2024), with first gold moved Q1 -> Q2 2025 (https://www.miningnewsnorth.com/story/2024/01/26/news/goose-gold-mine-costs-now-at-1-billion/8367.html ; https://www.miningweekly.com/article/b2gold-reaffirms-c154bn-development-estimate-for-goose-gold-project-eyes-mill-expansion-2025-03-28)
  • Goose first gold Jun 30, 2025 (last day of Q2); 2025 Goose guidance cut 120-150 -> 80-110 koz (Sep 2025, crushing constraints); 2026 outlook 'roughly 250 koz' (Sep 2025) became 170-200 koz after an April 2026 crusher fire (https://www.miningweekly.com/article/b2gold-trims-goose-output-guidance-but-reaffirms-2025-group-forecast-2025-09-15 ; https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/commodities/articles/b2gold-corp-btg-q2-2026-230115309.html)
  • Mali: 2024 guidance lowered mid-year (Fekola), 804.8 koz 'within the revised range'; Menankoto/Fekola Regional permit finally granted mid-2026 after years of delaysource
  • Consolidated guidance met on revised ranges in 2024 and 2025; 2026 narrowed to 820-920 koz with AISC $2,370-2,550 (Q2 2026)
  • Q2 2026: US$71M realised loss on gold collars, free cash flow -US$258M on cash taxes and gold prepays; cash US$287Msource

Boards today: Cinnamond: B2Gold + Onyx Gold + Contango Silver & Gold = 3 public roles (circular 2026). Johnson: chair emeritus only (no nominee listing).

Fit to this job
Company has built and operated open-pit gold mines in Namibia, Mali and the Philippines — same job. Arctic Nunavut (Goose, sealift logistics, winter ice road, crushing in cold) was new and is where the misses came. New CEO is a career CFO, not an operator; the executive chair is a lawyer/administrator by background.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. Cinnamond: 137,501 shares (~0.024%, ~US$1.7M), meets 3x salary requirement; sold ~77k shares Apr 1, 2026 (~US$356k, 20% of holdings). Johnson sold ~73k shares Mar 2026. Insiders net sellers ~US$10M/12 months. Cinnamond 2025 total comp as CFO ~US$2.46M; Johnson's 2025 CEO comp not extracted. Say-on-pay 2025: 93.2%. Sources: https://s204.q4cdn.com/324791784/files/doc_downloads/2026/04/B2Gold-MIC-FYE-December-31-2025.pdf ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nysemkt-btg/b2gold/management

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Goose capex ~2x B2Gold's own first estimate and ~2.5x Sabina's feasibility (C$610M, unverified); two production guidance cuts in its first year
  • Press-release headlines consistently lead with good news and bury cuts ('Remains On Track', 'Strong Operating Performance')
  • New CEO sold 20% of his holdings (Apr 2026) two months before taking the job; insiders net sellers US$10M over 12 months
  • Gold collar/prepay losses and negative free cash flow in a record gold price environment
  • Mali political/fiscal risk; Fekola is the biggest mine

Gate Growing into a ~US$4.1B valuation that already discounts Boumadine. At ~14× annualised EBITDA and ~24× forward earnings, Zgounder alone — 73 Moz of reserves, 11-year life, ~6 Moz/yr — does not carry the price; the market is paying for a US$3.5B PEA whose resource is 4.3 of 5.4 Moz AuEq Inferred, with a 22.6:1 strip, a roaster/payability chain untested at scale, and an FS that has already slipped from H1 to H2 2027. Funded to the next catalyst Funded through the FS from cash flow. The Boumadine build (PEA initial capex US$463M, sustaining US$507M) is not yet funded — plausibly from cash flow plus project debt if silver holds; an equity component is possible if it doesn't. No raise since Jun 2025.
Thesis

Zgounder, in Morocco's Anti-Atlas, is a ~3,900 tpd underground-plus-open-pit silver mine producing at a US$16.82/AgEq oz cash cost with 141 g/t feed and 91% recovery after a 2024 plant expansion. 2026 guidance 6.2–6.8 Moz AgEq (Zgounder 5.2–5.8 Moz Ag); H1 delivered 3.17 Moz AgEq, revenue US$214M, net income US$83.6M, operating cash flow US$118.6M.

Cash US$182.8M against ~US$80–85M of EBRD debt (being repaid early); no equity issued since the C$144M bought deal of Jun 2025. Silver is 93% of revenue — the cleanest silver beta on a major exchange (Nasdaq-listed May 2026, added to GDX).

The second leg is Boumadine: an updated PEA (Sep 9, 2026) shows after-tax NPV5% US$3.5B and 93% IRR at US$3,500 Au / US$50 Ag on US$463M initial capex, 8,000 tpd, 14 years, ~271 koz AuEq/yr — but it is gold-led by value (~58%), 80% Inferred, and a feasibility study is not due until H2 2027. 14 rigs turning; 145,000 m drilled YTD.

The Gate

Growing into a ~US$4.1B valuation that already discounts Boumadine. At ~14× annualised EBITDA and ~24× forward earnings, Zgounder alone — 73 Moz of reserves, 11-year life, ~6 Moz/yr — does not carry the price; the market is paying for a US$3.5B PEA whose resource is 4.3 of 5.4 Moz AuEq Inferred, with a 22.6:1 strip, a roaster/payability chain untested at scale, and an FS that has already slipped from H1 to H2 2027.

Sub-gates
  1. Zgounder grade — 2025 missed guidance (4.83 vs 5.0–5.3 Moz) on head grade of 145 g/t against 170–200 g/t guided; the reserve grade (145) sits below M&I (165) and the mill runs at ~140; H2 2026 strip ratio rises from ~10:1 to ~16:1, lifting cash cost toward the US$21.50 guide.
  2. Single-asset, single-country — Morocco is drafting a new mining law (May 2026) and is structurally drought-prone; Boumadine needs an ESIA.
  3. Beta — the stock is ~3× in twelve months with a ~3.3 beta; a silver pullback compresses the multiple before it touches the mine.

Read the September sell-off (−7% on Sep 23) as what happens to a 14× silver name when the metal wobbles — not as news about Zgounder.

← CheapestMost expensive →

Figure used: Zgounder AISC ~US$19/oz (management, 29 Sep — no AISC is published; Q2 cash cost US$16.82). On the cash-cost guide (~US$24.5 estimated AISC) it would be ~72nd — upper half either way.

Why mid-curve if it is cheap? Per silver-equivalent ounce Aya is the cheapest of the five silver names here (Fresnillo's silver mines ~US$26.6, First Majestic ~US$28.2, Avino ~US$38.75). But the industry curve subtracts gold, zinc and lead revenue, and a pure-silver mine has none to subtract — so mines with big by-products sit below it.

Improving: ~86th in 2025 → ~64th as cash costs fell (US$20.41 → US$16.82) while peers' rose. H2's higher strip ratio (10:1 → 16:1) pushes costs back toward guidance.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.

Detail
MetricHeadlineDetail
Risk score3/5A producing, net-cash, high-margin mine limits permanent loss; but one asset, one country, a 2025 guidance miss, an H2 cost step-up, and a valuation that needs a PEA-stage gold project to work. The loss path is de-rating, not insolvency.
Market cap2 Oct 2026: ~US$3.91B (C$38.68 · ~C$5.57B on 144.0M shares). ~C$5.7B / ~US$4.1B (C$39.72 on 23 Sep 2026; 144.0M shares; 52-wk C$11.95–43.12 — vendors disagree, some show C$6.15B). EV ~C$5.6B after ~US$100M net cash. P/E ~39× trailing, ~24× forward. Targets: Stifel C$56, Desjardins C$55, CIBC C$48, BMO C$46, NBF C$43 — consensus Buy ~C$44–48. No dividend, no buyback.
Capex / IRRBoumadine PEA (Sep 2026):Initial capex US$463M (incl. US$99M contingency), sustaining US$507M, 2-year build; after-tax IRR 93%, payback 0.7 yr at US$3,500 Au / US$50 Ag; 128% at spot (US$4,472 / US$66.85, 3 Sep). LOM AISC US$1,300/AuEq oz. 2026 group capex: US$36M Zgounder + ~US$60M exploration (230,000 m, later enlarged to 360,000 m at Boumadine over 2026–27).
NPVBoumadine after-tax NPV5% US$3.5B(base) / US$5.5B (spot) — up from US$1.475B in the 2025 PEA. That is roughly the entire enterprise value at base and more than it at spot, on a study that includes Inferred material. Zgounder: no NPV published in the Dec 2025 technical report; LOM ~66 Moz at US$16.26 cash cost.
DepositZgounder:P&P 15.7 Mt @ 145 g/t = 73.4 Moz Ag (Sep 2025, US$26); M&I 18.9 Mt @ 165 g/t = 100.2 Moz; Inf 4.5 Moz @ 340 g/t; life to 2036. Recent hits 3,501 g/t / 3.5 m, 783 g/t / 13 m; west-of-fault drilling from Q4. Boumadine: Ind. 8.6 Mt @ 4.02 g/t AuEq = 1.1 Moz; Inf 45.4 Mt @ 2.92 g/t = 4.3 Moz AuEq (Feb 2026; 121.7 g/t Ag, 1.93 g/t Au, 2.19% Zn, 1.01% Pb in Ind.); 5.4 km trend, open. Pyrite-stockpile reclaim adds ~1 Moz AgEq/yr for ~2 years.
NPV : capexBoumadine 7.6× at base, ~12× at spotThe highest ratio in either file by a distance, which is exactly what a PEA on 80% Inferred ounces at a 5% discount rate produces. Haircut to an 8% rate, Indicated-only tonnes and FS-level capex before believing it. Producer screen: gross margin 65.5% (Q2), OCF/revenue 50%; EV/oz P&P silver ~US$55 (US$4.0B ÷ 73 Moz) — expensive for the ounces, cheap only if Boumadine is real.
Valuation Anchor

~14× annualised Q2 EBITDA, ~24× forward P/E, ~US$55/oz on silver reserves. Zgounder at 6.5 Moz and a US$50/oz margin (which needs ~US$71.5 silver) earns ~US$325M a year; at 10× that is ~US$3.3B — roughly today's EV. At ~US$61 silver (1 Oct) the margin is ~US$37–39/oz, ~US$240–250M a year, ~US$2.4–2.5B at 10× — so Boumadine is carrying ~US$1.6B of the price. So Boumadine is in the price at a Boumadine-in-2030 discount rate, not a PEA discount rate.

The bull case is the spot NPV (US$5.5B) plus Zgounder; the bear case is silver at US$50 and an FS that trims the NPV to something a 22.6:1 strip and a roaster deserve.

Of the four producers this is the one whose valuation is most a call on a study rather than on cash flow — closer to NGEx in the copper file than to Pan American.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~1–2% after the January 2026 block sale (stale aggregators still show ~10%). CEO Benoit La Salle: 158,930 common shares + 1.8M options + 217k RSUs + 26k PSUs (C$6.9M total) — almost entirely granted; the cash-bought block is small. No La Salle family, Windiga or founder block exists. Director guideline 3× retainer. John Burzynski is the one director with genuine open-market buys (20k shares in 2025).
Insider activity (12 mo)
Large selling at the top. Jan 14–21, 2026: Chair Robert Taub sold 7.0M shares (~C$150M) and Lead Director Hambrecht ~0.5M in a secondary at C$21.47; both left the board at the June AGM. Management sold ~1.1M securities (~12% of holdings) alongside — La Salle 235k shares (~C$5M) [one source says 35k], Beaudoin, Landry-Tolszczuk, Ball, Burzynski. La Salle also sold 64k in mid-2025. No purchases by the CEO in 2025–26. The stock has since doubled from the sale price — the sellers were early, not wrong about the risk.
Strategic & prominent
Van Eck ~7.1% (10.2M shares, Aug 2026; was ~10% in 2024) — the largest holder, and GDX inclusion (Jun 2026) makes it a structural buyer. Global X (SIL) ~3.7%. Robert Taub's residual stake after the sale is undisclosed. No Sprott, Lundin, La Mancha or other strategic block.
Institutions / retail
2024 baseline: retail 57%, institutions 32%, insiders ~11%; post-Jan 2026 insiders ~1–2% and institutional share rising with the Nasdaq listing (US 13F coverage still thin; Canadian holders — Ninepoint, Mackenzie, RBC — not captured). 143.3M shares (Apr 2026), ~146M basic now. No buyback.

Read: This is the weakest ownership picture in the file for a US$4B company: the founding chair took C$150M off the table in January, the CEO's exposure is options, and nobody with a name has bought. The counter-argument is real — the stock doubled after they sold, and index flows (GDX, Nasdaq) now dominate — but insiders do not own the Boumadine story they are asking the market to pay 14× for.

Jurisdiction risk

National: better than its reputation, but concentrated. Morocco: Law 33-13, no mandatory state equity outside phosphates; Aya bought out ONHYM's 15% in 2022 (3% royalty remains); EBRD as lender; tax incentives keep 2025 government payments to ~C$2.3M. A new draft mining law (May 2026: safety, penalties, registry, permit reassignment) is not yet adopted and has no announced royalty change — watch it.

Local: low — no community disputes reported; water reservoirs full after a wet season, but the Anti-Atlas is structurally drought-prone and Boumadine's ESIA is still to come.

Single-asset, single-country is the real jurisdiction risk: there is no second mine to carry a bad year.

Differentiator
  1. Silver purity plus the lowest cost of the silver names per silver-equivalent ounce. 93% of revenue from silver at a US$17 cash cost with 141 g/t feed (on the industry's by-product curve it is mid-pack, ~64th percentile, because a pure-silver mine has no by-products to subtract — corrected 3 Oct from "first-quartile") — no other producer of this size offers that combination; Pan American and Coeur are gold companies with silver brands.
  2. Net cash and self-funded growth — H1 OCF US$119M, no equity since 2025, EBRD debt being retired early.
  3. Boumadine's scale — a 5.4 km mineralised trend with 14 rigs on it, 271 koz AuEq/yr in the PEA, a second company inside the first.
  4. Nasdaq listing and GDX inclusion (2026) — index flows that small silver names never get.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is silver purity, and Boumadine — the growth leg the price depends on — is a gold project by value. If it gets built, Aya becomes a balanced Au/Ag producer and the purity premium goes away. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, district-scale · moves the needle: high. Boumadine: 145,719 m YTD, 14 rigs, 360,000 m infill plus 40,000 m step-out through 2027 — the FS depends on converting Inferred, so this is conversion drilling that is the thesis. Zgounder near-mine (16,217 m YTD; 4,770 g/t / 2.4 m) targets life extension beyond 2036 and the west-of-fault block from Q4 2026.

More Boumadine ounces matter less than Indicated Boumadine ounces.

Next Catalyst

Q3 production (Oct) — inventory catch-up sales and the first quarter of ~16:1 strip; Boumadine infill results through 2027 and an updated MRE; Boumadine FS H2 2027 (slipped once) with ESIA; infrastructure ground-breaking "end of 2026"; tertiary crusher early 2027 (3,850 tpd steady state); Moroccan mining-law adoption.

Open Questions
  • What does Zgounder actually grade through 2027 — 145 g/t (reserve) or 165 g/t (M&I) — and does 2026 guidance hold at a doubling strip ratio?
  • How much of Boumadine's 4.3 Moz AuEq Inferred converts, and what happens to NPV at an 8% rate with FS-level capex?
  • Does the roaster / concentrate payability chain (Au 82%, Ag 85%) hold at 8,000 tpd?
  • Can Aya fund a US$463M+ build from cash flow, or does Boumadine bring back the equity market?
  • Does the draft Moroccan mining law change royalties or permit tenure?
  • At what silver price does the market stop paying 14× — and how much of the stock's 3× move was the metal?

Zgounder 1.49 Moz Ag (record, +43% y/y) at 3,889 tpd, 141 g/t, 91.2% recovery; consolidated 1.68 Moz AgEq. Revenue US$96.8M (−17% q/q on a 22% lower realised price of US$64.22; a third of production sold into the June dip). Net income US$35.0M; OCF US$48.4M; cash US$182.8M.

Aside

Stock ~3× in twelve months; beta ~3.3. Uncertain items: exact total debt at Jun 30 (est. US$80–85M), vendor market-cap discrepancy, FS timing (company documents say both H1 and H2 2027).

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 1/5

Built Zgounder on budget and 2026 is running to plan: the team has proved it can deliver a mine. Held at B, not higher, because two straight years of missed production guidance went out under 'record' headlines and the 2025 pay vote failed. Candour stays 2 — the test is whether 2026 guidance is met and said plainly.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Benoit La Salle (President & CEO, director, since April 2020): Age 71. Founder and long-time CEO of SEMAFO (West Africa gold); founder of Sama Resources. · Ghislane Guedira (Chair (nominated 2026, replacing Robert Taub), since 2026): Casablanca-based; CEO of A.P.M. Capital Morocco. · Raphaël Beaudoin (VP Operations, since unverified): Fronts strip-ratio and underground-rate questions on calls.
Track record
  • La Salle founded SEMAFO (1995) and ran it to 2012; SEMAFO built the Mana mine in Burkina Faso and was later sold to Endeavour (2020, after his departure) — a mine-building hit in the 2005-12 cycle (background widely reported; outcome details unverified in this pass)
  • Sama Resources (La Salle founder/chair): Ivory Coast Ni-Cu explorer, still an explorer after ~15 years — no exit (board listed in circular: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1826836/000162828026034708/ags-micx2026xedgar2025x05x.htm)
  • Zgounder expansion built for ~US$166M, reported on budget, but commissioning slipped from late Q2-2024 to commercial production late Q4-2024 after an EPC ball-mill hydraulic fault; 2024 guidance cut on 6 Sep 2024 to 1.6-1.8Mozsource
  • 2025: produced 4.83Moz Ag vs 5.0-5.3Moz guidance, head grade 145 g/t vs 170-200 g/t guided; press release led with 'record December'source
  • 2026: H1 2.8Moz at Zgounder vs 5.2-5.8Moz guide; cash cost US$17.69/oz in Q2 vs US$21.50 guide; guidance maintained; cash US$183M, no financingsource
  • Say-on-pay FAILED at the 2025 AGM (45.6% for); 2025 CEO pay ~$23.6M, of which ~$18.8M option grant value (circular)

Boards today: La Salle: Aya (CEO/director), Sama Resources, Falcon Energy Materials plc — 3 public roles.

Fit to this job
La Salle has built and run a mine in Africa before (SEMAFO/Mana, open-pit gold) and has now expanded and operated Zgounder (underground+open-pit silver, Morocco) for two years. New for the team: Boumadine is a polymetallic (Au-Ag-Zn-Pb) project with a much larger build than Zgounder, feasibility due H1-2027; the Sept 2026 Cu-Ag portfolio acquisition adds a new commodity.
Skin & pay
1/5 — under ~0.5%, options only, or net sellers while promoting. La Salle owns 158,930 shares (0.11%) plus 216,904 RSUs and 1.8M options — equity mostly from grants, no open-market buying found. 2025 total pay ~$23.6M (salary $446k, bonus $373k, RSUs $4.0M, options $18.8M; currency as per circular). Say-on-pay 45.6% for in 2025. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1826836/000162828026034708/ags-micx2026xedgar2025x05x.htm

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Two consecutive annual production guidance misses (2024 cut, 2025 missed) with upbeat headlines each time.
  • Failed say-on-pay 2025; CEO 2025 pay ~$23.6M (mostly options) while holding only 0.11% of shares outright.
  • CEO is 71 and sits on two other public boards; succession not visible.
  • Financials: G&A jumped to US$7.9M in Q2 2026 from ~US$3M a quarter, on top of US$13.9M of share-based pay in FY25 - watch whether it stays there in Q3.

What the numbers say
  1. The Zgounder expansion changed the company: revenue US$39M (FY24, with a US$27M impairment and a loss) → US$202M (FY25) → US$214M in H1 2026 alone; gross margin 69% vs 14% in FY24; cash cost down to US$16.8/oz AgEq.
  2. Cash US$49.8M (end 2023) → low of US$18.3M (Mar 2025) → US$182.8M (Jun 2026). The June 2025 C$144M bought deal bridged the gap; since then operations fund everything (H1 2026 operating cash flow US$119M, ~US$80M free cash flow).
  3. Money now goes into the ground at Boumadine (US$42M in FY25, US$25M in H1 2026) while mill capex fell to ~US$15M in H1 2026; EBRD debt is being repaid (US$112M → US$84M).
  4. Shares 122M (end 2023) → 144M (+18%) through two bought deals; no dividends or buybacks. G&A jumped to US$7.9M in Q2 2026 and share-based pay is heavy (US$13.9M in FY25).
  5. Watch: no AISC is disclosed (only cash cost per ounce), Moroccan tax takes ~37% of pre-tax profit, and the 2024 cash-flow comparatives were restated.

Thesis

Diablillos, on the Salta–Catamarca border at ~4,000 m, is a large oxide silver-gold system (Oculto, JAC and satellites) that AbraSilver has grown from a modest historical resource to M&I 248 Moz Ag + 2.54 Moz Au (Apr 2026) at a discovery cost of ~US$0.10/oz AgEq. The DFS (Jun 2026, Worley): 9,000 tpd open pit and tank leach, 25-year life, years 1–5 averaging 13.9 Moz Ag + 89 koz Au (20.3 Moz AgEq) at AISC US$19.69, initial capex US$721.5M (15.5% contingency), after-tax NPV5% US$3.0B and IRR 41.9% at US$50 Ag / US$3,650 Au; US$4.8B / 56.5% at spot; US$1.9B / 31.4% at the US$40 / US$2,920 downside. Reserves 183.5 Moz Ag + 1.76 Moz Au. Everything that can be de-risked on paper has been: both provincial environmental approvals (Salta Apr 27, Catamarca Jun 24, 2026), RIGI adhesion (Resolution 562/2026 — 25% income tax, 0% export duties, 30-year stability, FX freedom), a Kolla community public hearing without opposition, and a Worley bridging-engineering contract. What is not done: the money. FID has slipped from Q4 2026 → Q2 2027 → "H2 2027"; no debt, stream or partner is announced.

Cash ~C$70M net after a C$50M raise at C$14.70 in July. Kinross (4%) has participation rights and a ROFO on new Argentine projects; Eric Sprott ~8%. Central Puerto sold its entire 9.9% on Sep 16 for C$228M (a US$138M gain) and the stock fell 22% in a week. CEO John Miniotis; Executive Chair Marie Inkster (ex-Lundin Mining CEO). Five analysts, all Buy, avg target C$21.20; company NAVPS C$26 base / C$42 spot.

The company's own language is "equity, debt, strategic partnerships or JV"; nothing is signed, and the FID has moved out twice.

Sub-gates
  1. The anchor left — Central Puerto's clean exit of 9.9% (Sep 16) removed the only Argentine strategic and triggered a domestic political row about RIGI-linked windfalls; Kinross at 4% is a participant, not a partner.
  2. Capex creep — US$544M (PFS, Dec 2024) → US$722M (DFS, Jun 2026), AISC US$12.67 → US$19.98/oz AgEq.

The DFS deck is the tell: US$50 silver was chosen when spot was US$70. A study that needs today's prices to look good is a study whose financing depends on today's prices holding.

Valuation Anchor

~0.5× NAV at the DFS deck (~0.3× at spot) on a permitted, RIGI-approved, reserve-backed 25-year mine — the largest defined discount in the file that is actually computable. The re-rate path is textbook: financing package (H1 2027) → FID (H2 2027) → construction → producer multiple; developers at this stage in tier-one Latin American provinces have historically moved from ~0.5× to ~0.8–1.0× NAV through that sequence, which is 1.6–2× on progress alone and 2.5–3.5× if silver holds US$69+.

The bear case is not the mine — it is the terms: a US$720M package at US$40 silver built from a stream on the gold, a project loan with hedging, and equity at a lower price than July's C$14.70, leaving shareholders with less of a bigger pie.

Bucket: scale & financing — the Solaris archetype from the copper file: fully permitted, technically done, one big cheque away.

Read: Two real votes and one loud exit. Sprott has bought twice and held through dilution; Kinross has bought at every price up to C$14.70 — that is a major saying the asset is real at four times the entry price. Against that, Central Puerto took US$163M off the table in a single day and management sold ~C$6.6M within weeks of publishing the DFS. The register is telling you the asset is good and the next twelve months are hard; both are true.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the best Argentina has offered a miner in thirty years. Milei's coalition won the Oct 2025 midterms; RIGI is law and Diablillos is approved under it (US$482M investment, 25% tax, 0% export duties, 30-year stability, FX freedom phasing to 100% by year 4); export duties on all mining already 0% since Aug 2025; the Apr 2026 glacier-law reform handed periglacial oversight to provinces — helpful at 4,000 m, and being litigated. Mining exports +74% in H1 2026. The risk is reversal: RIGI is a Milei policy, and a Sep 2026 political row over Central Puerto's RIGI-linked gain shows the opposition's line of attack.

Provincial / local: strong. Salta is the Fraser Institute's top Latin American jurisdiction; both Salta and Catamarca issued DIAs within two months of each other and ratified an inter-provincial cooperation agreement; the Kolla community of Santa Rosa de los Pastos Grandes attended the public hearing without recorded opposition. Physical constraints are the local issue: 4,000 m, water (60 L/s), solar-diesel power, contract mining, a 2.5-year build in the Puna.

Same national tailwind as Argenta, one valley over; a far more advanced project, and therefore far more exposed if the tailwind reverses.

Differentiator
  1. Everything except the money is done — permits, RIGI, DFS, reserves, engineering partner, land, community. No other developer in this file has both environmental approvals, a fiscal-stability regime and a definitive feasibility study in hand simultaneously.
  2. Scale and life — 25 years, 20 Moz AgEq/yr in the first five, 366 Moz AgEq of reserves, with a 130 Mt heap-leach resource (PEA Q4 2026) and Oculto West / Cerro Viejo drilling outside the pit as free options.
  3. A team that has sold companies and run a major — Miniotis (AuRico → Centerra), Inkster (Lundin Mining CEO), Weyland (Lundin/Kinross), a project director from Lydian and AngloGold; plus Kinross on the register with participation rights.
  4. The cleanest multiple in the file — 0.5× NAV, no warrants, no debt, five Buy ratings, a C$50M raise done at C$14.70 with no discount to the market.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a de-risked, buildable, US$720M project) and the gate (financing US$720M) are the same fact. And the two things that happened after the DFS — insiders selling and the anchor exiting — are the market's own read of how hard the next step is.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, expanding beyond the pit · moves the needle: medium. Phase VI (15,000 m, fully funded, three rigs by September) is finding ounces outside the DFS pit: Oculto West 109 m @ 221 g/t Ag / 0.72 g/t Au, Condoryacu 72 m @ 18.7 g/t Au + 2.1% Cu from surface, Cerro Viejo (new gold target 4 km north). With 454 Moz AgEq M&I already, more ounces extend life and support a second phase (water permitting); they do not change the financing question. La Coipita (Cu-Au, Teck earn-in to 80%) is a free option.

The next MRE (early 2027) and heap-leach PEA (Q4 2026) matter for the expansion case, not the FID.

Next Catalyst

Financing package — debt / stream / partner (undated; the whole re-rate); heap-leach PEA (Q4 2026); early works and long-lead procurement (funded from July raise); Phase VI results through Q4 and an updated MRE (early 2027); FID H2 2027 (slipped twice); Central Puerto's exit fully absorbed; any Argentine political move against RIGI.

Open Questions
  • What does the financing package look like — how much stream, how much debt, at what silver price, and how much equity at what price?
  • Who buys Central Puerto's 9.9%, and does Kinross step up from 4% or stay a passenger?
  • What does the DFS look like at reserve prices (US$29.50 / US$2,800) — does the IRR still clear 25%?
  • Why did the FID slip from Q4 2026 to H2 2027 within nine months, and is H2 2027 real?
  • Does the water plan (60 L/s) survive a 25-year, 9,000 tpd operation in the Puna — and what does an expansion cost in water rights?
  • Can this team build a US$720M mine at 4,000 m on schedule, having never built one?

What is NEW: building a US$722M open-pit, agitated-leach silver-gold mine. Neither CEO nor COO has been the construction executive on a mine build; Weyland's experience is studies and due diligence at a major. Inkster adds operator credibility but as chair, not builder. Red flags

  • Project financing (Q4 2026 target) and FID (Q2 2027) not yet done — the biggest promises are still open.

Simplified from the original filings (last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years, C$ millions, fiscal year ends 31 Dec). Every column links to the statements it came from.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash plus term deposits were C$23.5M at 30 June 2026, and a July 2026 C$50M bought deal lifts liquidity to about C$70M, roughly 12 months of runway.
  2. Over the last 8 quarters C$95M went into the ground and C$16.2M into cash overhead, so overhead is about 14% of spend.
  3. Burn has doubled to C$11–13M of exploration a quarter; cash G&A rose to C$2.0–3.7M a quarter and share-based pay hit C$7.3M in 2025.
  4. Shares outstanding rose from 113.3M in December 2023 to 165.5M in August 2026, up 46%, after about C$190M of equity raised, all at rising prices.
  5. No debt remains after the final US$6.85M Diablillos payment in April 2025; the 2024 going-concern note was dropped in 2025, and key management pay was C$3.3M in H1 2026.

The best-funded, highest-margin silver build on the market — with a feasibility study, US$406M of cash and no permit, and a site that has been closed since ten workers were abducted in January

Gate Reopening the site and receiving the MIA — two things outside the company's control, in the state that hosts Mexico's most violent cartel war. Every economic number is excellent and every operational number since January is zero. The construction decision was guided for H2 2026 "on permit receipt"; the permit is overdue, SEMARNAT granted three environmental approvals in all of 2025, the 2023 mining-law regulation is still unpublished, and the Sheinbaum government has opened a labour-conditions probe into the company after the abductions. Sub-gates: (1) the bulk sample — the 10,000 t reconciliation test that was to validate grade and ground conditions before construction was never completed; (2) the accusation — ex-workers told CBC that local management coordinated with armed groups; the company categorically denies it, but the FGR is investigating; (3) the timeline — H2 2027 first silver assumes a 2026 restart that has not happened; each quarter of suspension pushes production and burns ~US$20M; (4) the royalty — a 2–3.5% NSR now sits with Elemental (no buyback), after Vizsla Royalties was sold for C$327M in September.

Funded to the next catalyst Fully funded for the build — the only developer in the file that is. The risk is not a raise; it is that suspension burn erodes the cushion (~8 quarters of idle burn before cash falls below capex) while the permit waits.
Thesis

Panuco, in the Sierra Madre 40 km from Mazatlán, is a high-grade epithermal vein district consolidated by Vizsla since 2019 — 413,000 m drilled, 1,100 holes. The feasibility study (Nov 2025) is the strongest set of numbers in this file: initial capex US$239M, after-tax NPV5% US$1.80B and IRR 111% at US$35.50 Ag / US$3,100 Au, payback 7 months, AISC US$10.61/oz AgEq, 17.4 Moz AgEq/yr over 9.4 years from reserves of 102.7 Moz Ag + 829 koz Au at 416 g/t AgEq. It is fully funded: US$406.5M cash (Jul 31, 2026) after a US$115M equity raise (Jun 2025) and US$300M of 5% convertible notes (Nov 2025, conversion US$5.84), plus an undrawn FIFOMI working-capital line. Engineering and procurement are underway — M3 (EPCM), Mining Plus/Byrnecut (mine design), FLSmidth (eight equipment packages) — targeting a construction decision in H2 2026 and first silver in H2 2027. Then January 2026: ten Mexican employees were abducted at gunpoint from the Concordia compound; nine are confirmed dead, one missing; the Sinaloa Cartel's Chapitos faction mistook them for rivals. The site has been suspended since Jan 23 — no drilling, no underground development, no bulk-sample results — and the environmental permit (MIA, filed Q1 2025, guided "mid-2026") has not arrived. CEO Michael Konnert and Chair Craig Parry (Inventa Capital); new Mexico president and government-relations VP hired 2026. Analysts: NBF and CIBC downgraded in Feb–Mar; no coverage updates in 90 days.

The Gate

Reopening the site and receiving the MIA — two things outside the company's control, in the state that hosts Mexico's most violent cartel war. Every economic number is excellent and every operational number since January is zero. The construction decision was guided for H2 2026 "on permit receipt"; the permit is overdue, SEMARNAT granted three environmental approvals in all of 2025, the 2023 mining-law regulation is still unpublished, and the Sheinbaum government has opened a labour-conditions probe into the company after the abductions.

Sub-gates
  1. The bulk sample — the 10,000 t reconciliation test that was to validate grade and ground conditions before construction was never completed.
  2. The accusation — ex-workers told CBC that local management coordinated with armed groups; the company categorically denies it, but the FGR is investigating.
  3. The timeline — H2 2027 first silver assumes a 2026 restart that has not happened; each quarter of suspension pushes production and burns ~US$20M.
  4. The royalty — a 2–3.5% NSR now sits with Elemental (no buyback), after Vizsla Royalties was sold for C$327M in September.

The FS is not the gate. The FS is done. The question is whether a mine can be built and staffed in Concordia municipality in 2027.

Risk score3/5A feasibility study, 102 Moz of reserves, US$406M of cash against US$239M of capex, and a fully-engineered plant limit the permanent-loss case severely: the money is in the bank and the deposit is real. A 3 rather than a 2 because the site has been closed for eight months after nine employees were murdered, the permit is overdue in a hostile permitting regime, and no one can put a date on either. The loss path is a permanent security discount and a year of slippage, not insolvency.

Valuation Anchor

~0.7× NAV at a stale deck, ~0.4× at spot, on a fully-funded, feasibility-stage, 111%-IRR project — the cheapest defined ounces in the file, and the market is not wrong to price them that way. The discount is not Mexico in the abstract; it is Concordia, Sinaloa, specifically — a site the company itself has not reopened in eight months.

The bull case: MIA arrives, site restarts under new security arrangements, construction decision in H1 2027, first silver 2028, and the stock re-rates toward 0.8–1.0× a spot NAV of US$3B+ — a 2–3× from here on progress alone.

The bear case: a permanent 40–50% security discount, a permit that arrives late or with conditions, and a workforce that will not come back — in which case US$406M of cash is the floor and the equity trades on it. Bucket: cheap defined ounces — reserves, FS, funded; the discount is one variable (site/permit), legible and binary.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~5.5% (insiders; aggregators range 5.5–7.9%). Chair Craig Parry 4.6M shares / 1.3% + 2.1M options (down from 8.3M / 4.0% in 2023); CEO Michael Konnert 2.5M / 0.7% + 4.7M options; COO Simon Cmrlec 1.2M. Founder shares from the 2018–19 Inventa era plus option exercises; the founders have been reducing. CEO FY26 comp ~US$2.6M incl. equity.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net selling, badly timed. Konnert sold 310,000 @ C$7.78–8.22 (Jan 9 & 12, 2026; ~C$2.4M, ~11% of holding) and Cmrlec 500,000 @ C$7.79 (Jan 9; C$3.9M) — two weeks before the abduction and the 41% drawdown. Buys: director Pokrandt 170k (Nov–Dec 2025, ~C$1.2M); director Cobbold 89k (Jun 2026). Twelve months to Jan 2026: insiders bought C$1.3M, sold C$7.0M.
Strategic & prominent
No 10%+ holder. Eric Sprott put C$10M in the 2020 placement (last filing Apr 2022: 5.2M shares + 5.3M warrants, 3.5%); no disclosure since — current stake unknown. Institutions ~52% of the register (158 filers): Sprott Inc 4.9%, Tidal/SILJ 3.9% and adding (Sep 2026), Franklin 3.8%, Global X 3.7%, Van Eck 3.7%, Jupiter 2.8%, Vanguard 2.7%, Waratah, Fourth Sail, Ninepoint, Mackenzie. Macquarie's mining vice-chair sits on the board (Macquarie held a US$220M project-finance mandate in 2025, since superseded by the converts). No Rule, Gentile, Palisades or Crescat found.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~52%, insiders ~5%, retail ~43%. 355.0M shares; FD ~379M; US$300M converts → 51.4M shares at US$5.84 (capped call to US$10.51). Inventa Capital (Parry/Konnert) incubated Vizsla Silver, Vizsla Copper and Vizsla Royalties; no fees paid to Inventa by VZLA.

Read: A founder-led, institution-owned register where the founders have been quietly selling into strength for two years and sold C$6.3M two weeks before the worst event in the company's history. Nobody with a name has bought the drawdown; the buyers are silver ETFs. Read the ownership as 'index money on a project the insiders were already trimming' — not as a vote against the asset, but not as a vote for it either.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the hardest permitting regime in the file, in a country with no new concessions. Sheinbaum has reiterated no new mining concessions; Camimex counts three environmental permits granted in 2025 and ~US$11B of projects waiting; the 2023 mining-law reform (30-year concessions, water prerequisite, community benefit-sharing) has been upheld by the Supreme Court but its regulation is still unpublished; an open-pit ban bill is pending (Panuco is underground). Panuco's MIA is caught in exactly this queue.

Local: the worst security layer in either file, by an order of magnitude. The Chapitos–Mayos war since the Sep 2024 Zambada rendition has made Culiacán and Concordia municipality a battlefield: mass displacement, up to 15,000 troops, US FTO designation, and in April 2026 US indictments of ten Sinaloa politicians including the sitting governor. Vizsla's ten workers were killed in that war. The five ejido agreements (30 years) are intact and there is no community opposition — the community is the victim. Water is from underground dewatering; the TSF is conventional slurry, not dry-stack.

Same country as Avino and Coeur's Mexican mines; not the same risk. Durango and Chihuahua are not Concordia.

Differentiator
  1. Economics nobody else in the file can match — and cash to build them. A 111% IRR, 7-month payback, US$10.61 AISC, 416 g/t AgEq reserves, and US$406M in the bank against US$239M of capex: the only developer here that needs no financing, no partner and no stream to reach production.
  2. Execution is procured — EPCM (M3), mine contractor (Byrnecut), equipment (FLSmidth) all under contract or mandate; this is a project waiting for permission, not for engineering.
  3. District scale behind the reserve — 128.8 Moz Ag + 1.04 Moz Au M&I plus 74 Moz Inferred, 413,000 m of drilling, a new discovery (Animas) and the Fresnillo ground added in December.
  4. Balanced metal — ~60% silver / 40% gold means it is silver torque with a gold floor, and the only silver developer here with reserves in the Measured category.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is a built-and-funded project in a district the cartel controls; the FS numbers are why the stock is US$1.4B and the site closure is why it isn't US$3B. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, district-scale · moves the needle: medium — but paused. 2026 was to be a 60,000 m year with 13,000 m of underground infill from the 480 level; effectively nothing has been drilled since January. Animas (897 g/t AgEq / 5.8 m) and the San Dimas corridor land package are the upside; Copala at depth and Napoleon are the reserve-conversion targets. With 129 Moz M&I already, exploration adds mine life, not the investment case.

The resource is not the constraint. Access is.

Next Catalyst

Site restart (no date); MIA receipt (guided mid-2026, overdue); construction decision (guided H2 2026, will slip); mining-contract award; Byrnecut NTP; bulk-sample / reconciliation results; Q2 FY27 results (Dec) — cash burn and any suspension update; FGR investigation outcome; new coverage after two downgrades.

Open Questions
  • When does the site reopen, under what security arrangements, and who staffs it — the same Concordia workforce, or contractors flown in?
  • Does the MIA arrive in 2026, and with what conditions, in a regime that granted three in 2025?
  • Is there anything to the ex-workers' allegation that local management coordinated with an armed group — and what does the FGR conclude?
  • What did the 10,000 t bulk sample show, or was it never processed?
  • At what point does US$20M/quarter of burn with no site activity start to erode the 'fully funded' claim?
  • Why did the CEO and COO sell ~C$6.3M of stock two weeks before the abduction — and has any insider bought since?
Context & updates
3 Oct 2026 refresh

Site still closed. On 29 Sep the CEO said the aim is to be back on site by end-2026 with a temporary camp that houses an army barracks, and re-guided the environmental permit (MIA) and land-use change to Q4 2026–Q1 2027 (was mid-2026). No construction decision yet; the company still targets first silver H2 2027 / first pour mid-2028.

Abduction (Jan 23, 2026) and aftermath

Ten employees taken from the Concordia compound; bodies recovered from a clandestine grave near El Verde; 9 confirmed dead by Apr 6, 1 missing. Chapitos regional boss arrested Jun 2; two more Sep 9. Site suspended since; engineering continues remotely. Stock −41% in two weeks. Nationwide miner protests Feb 14; FGR probe of labour conditions; company denies extortion, ransom or coordination.

Q1 FY27 (Jul 31, 2026; MD&A Sep 4)

Cash US$406.5M (−US$20.8M in the quarter); net loss US$19.8M; no drilling, no UG development; convertible notes US$300M face. "Construction decision subject to completion of permitting." Chief Geologist resigned Aug 27.

Procurement (Apr–Jun 2026)

M3 Engineering EPCM (~US$170M scope); Mining Plus / Byrnecut mine design (US$50M development capex + US$40M ore development pre-production); FLSmidth eight equipment packages sized for 3,300/4,000 tpd. FIFOMI MXN 173M (~US$10M) working-capital line, undrawn.

Royalty (Sep 15, 2026)

Elemental Royalty completed the C$327M acquisition of Vizsla Royalties — a 2.0–3.5% NSR on Panuco with no buyback — so the royalty is now held by a third party. Vizsla no longer holds VROY.

Aside

The FS deck (US$35.50 Ag) is now about half of spot; every published multiple is on stale prices. Insider sales by the CEO (310k @ C$7.78–8.22) and COO (500k @ C$7.79) on Jan 9–12 preceded the incident by two weeks.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 3/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Real builders hired and fully funded; the founders are financiers with several roles who sold stock in the drawdown, and permit dates have drifted via conference remarks.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Michael Konnert (President, CEO & Founder, since Sept 2017 (founded Vizsla; Panuco optioned 2019)): Deal-maker/financier: co-founder and managing partner of Inventa Capital (raised >C$800M); co-founded CobaltOne Energy (2017, acquired by Blackstone Minerals — small). Also executive chairman of Vizsla Royalties, director of Vizsla Copper and Summa Silver. · Craig Parry (Chairman (founder), since Dec 2018): Geologist; Rio Tinto 2000-08; co-founder NexGen Energy (Arrow discovery) and IsoEnergy (Hurricane); lead director Skeena Resources; executive chairman & CEO Vizsla Copper. Serial founder with several concurrent roles. · Simon Cmrlec (COO & Director, since Director since formation; COO appointed 2024/25 (date unverified)): 30+ yrs; former COO of Ausenco (EPCM builder of many plants); Olympic Dam (WMC), Goro Nickel project manager (Inco). The genuine mine-builder on the team. · Dave D'Antonio, P.Eng. (SVP Technical Services, since unverified (2025)): Ex head of mine technical services at K92 Kainantu; OceanaGold Didipio — underground operations experience. · Luis Lázaro (President, Mexico, since unverified): Mexican industrial CEO (Citrofrut, CEMEX ops) — not a miner.
Track record
  • Konnert: built Vizsla from an option deal (2019) to a C$1.9B company with a feasibility study (Nov 2025) and US$450M cash — explorer-to-FS job done once, heresource
  • Konnert's prior company CobaltOne Energy was acquired by Blackstone Minerals (small, outcome value not verified)source
  • Parry: NexGen (Arrow) and IsoEnergy (Hurricane) are major uranium discoveries from the 2013-2022 cycle; neither has been built or sold yet; Tigers Realm Coal (ASX) went nowhere for shareholderssource
  • Cmrlec: COO of Ausenco — a contractor that has delivered multiple precious-metal process plants; his personal project record at Vizsla is untestedsource
  • Spin-outs: Vizsla Copper (2021) and Vizsla Royalties (2024) — Konnert/Parry hold executive roles at both; value creation for VZLA shareholders from these not quantifiedsource

Boards today: Konnert: Vizsla Silver (CEO), Vizsla Royalties (exec chair), Vizsla Copper (director), Summa Silver (director) = 4. Parry: Vizsla Silver (chair), Vizsla Copper (exec chair & CEO), Skeena (lead director), plus Surge Copper/Gold Bull/Outback Goldfields per 2023 circular = 5-6. Both are stretched across several companies while Panuco heads into construction.

Fit to this job
Same stage done once by this team (explorer→FS, here). Mexico: Konnert/Parry had no prior Mexican operating history; they hired for it (Lázaro, Hernandez, Gómez Olmos ex-FIFOMI). Underground narrow-vein silver-gold at ~4,000 tpd is new for the executives; Cmrlec (plant builder) and D'Antonio (underground technical) cover the gap on paper. What is NEW and unproven: running a mine site in cartel-contested Sinaloa after 10 workers were abducted and 9 killed in Jan 2026 — this is now a security-management job none of them has done.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. CEO Konnert ~0.77% (~C$14.8M), chairman Parry holdings not quantified; both net sellers over the last 12 months (Konnert -C$3.8M, Parry -C$2.0M). Only notable insider buy: director Harry Pokrandt C$1.0M at C$7.09 (Dec 2025). CFO exercised 225k options at C$2.31 (June 2026). CEO total comp US$2.07M, 15% salary / 85% bonus-equity (SimplyWall.st, latest year) — ~0.15% of a C$1.9B market cap. 2023 circular shows 208M shares then; current D&O group % not retrieved.source

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Insiders net sellers of ~C$11M in 12 months: CEO Konnert net seller C$3.8M, chairman Parry net seller C$2.0M (sold 217k sh at C$5.14 June 2026) — during the post-abduction drawdown.
  • Timeline drift communicated in conference remarks rather than a plain revised-guidance release; H2-2027 first silver and mid-2028 first pour coexist.
  • CEO and chairman each hold 4-6 public roles including sister companies (Vizsla Copper, Vizsla Royalties).
  • Site inaccessible since late Jan 2026; the security problem is structural (Sinaloa cartel conflict), not a one-off.
  • CEO comp US$2.07M (85% equity/bonus) at a pre-construction developer.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash was US$406.5M at 31 July 2026 after a US$300M 5% convertible note and US$126.7M of equity in FY26; that covers years until Panuco construction starts.
  2. Overhead is large and growing: FY26 cash G&A was US$16.2M plus US$10.9M of share-based pay, against US$32.8M of capitalised exploration, about a third of spend.
  3. In Q1 FY27 overhead exceeded in-ground spending as capitalised exploration dropped to US$3.1M while spend shifts to engineering and holding costs.
  4. Shares outstanding rose from 232.6M in April 2024 to 355.0M in July 2026, up 53%; the notes could add 51.4M shares on conversion at US$5.84.
  5. Quarterly net income is dominated by fair-value swings on the notes' conversion feature, a US$49.5M derivative at FY26 year-end; the first US$9.6M coupon was paid in July 2026.

Thesis

Los Ricos South, in the Hostotipaquillo district of Jalisco, is a high-grade silver-gold underground project (with a late-life open pit) that GoGold has advanced since 2019 alongside Parral, a Chihuahua tailings-reprocessing operation that has thrown off cash since 2014 (FY2025: 2.15 Moz AgEq, US$72.5M revenue, US$25.7M operating cash flow). The FS (Jan 2025): initial capex US$227M, after-tax NPV5% US$355M and IRR 28% at US$26.80 Ag / US$2,330 Au — a deck now less than half of spot; 7.3 Moz AgEq/yr in years 1–5 at AISC US$11.19; 15-year life; reserves 47.8 Moz Ag + 457 koz Au at 145 g/t / 1.39 g/t; 2,000 tpd long-hole with paste fill. After a permit wait that ran from "mid-2024" to Jun 8, 2026 (SEMARNAT approvals granted; board approved construction the same day), the build began Aug 25, 2026: M3 as EPCM, >150 contractors on site, plant design 90%, all long-lead orders placed (SAG mill May 2027 is the critical path), Cominvi mobilising underground in Q4, powerline Nov 2026, portal and paste plant Jan 2027, first pour Q2 2028. Funding: US$284M cash and no debt, stream, royalty or offtake — from two bought deals (C$86M at C$1.82, Apr 2025; C$144M at C$2.65, Nov 2025) plus Parral cash flow; the company models cash never falling below US$130M through the build. Los Ricos North (PEA 2023: NPV US$413M, 110 Moz AgEq) is the sequel, to be permitted around first pour. CEO Brad Langille built Ocampo and El Cubo (Gammon Gold) and Parral in 18 months. Three analysts, all Buy at C$5.50; stock C$4.34.

The Gate

Building a 2,000 tpd underground mine on time and on a US$227M budget struck in January 2025 — in Jalisco, during a cartel succession war. The FS capex has not been revised for 2025–26 inflation or peso strength; an internal ~US$260M figure circulates unverified. Execution risk is concentrated in two places management itself names: bulk sub-level stoping in and around the historic Cinco Minas workings (ground conditions), and the SAG mill delivery (54-week lead, May 2027).

Sub-gates
  1. The permit's fine print — the June release says "all permits and approvals required from SEMARNAT"; it does not itemise land-use change, SEDENA explosives or CONAGUA water, and Mexico's MIA processing still runs 12–15 months with the 2023 mining-law regulation unpublished.
  2. Jalisco — CJNG's leader was killed at Tapalpa in February 2026, triggering statewide roadblocks and a succession fight; TD Cowen named Los Ricos as Jalisco-exposed; no incident at site, but Endeavour's Terronera — the nearest analogue — was shut for eleven days by an ejido blockade in August.
  3. Parral is the bridge and it is ageing — Q3 FY26 AISC US$40.78/oz (from US$23.72 in FY25) with four to five years of tailings left.
  4. The price — at C$1.89B the market has moved from 0.4× to something near 1× a spot NAV; the re-rate for permit + funding + construction start has largely happened.

This is the file's first genuinely de-risked developer — and the first where the question is 'what is left to earn?' rather than 'what could go wrong?'

Producer-style screens for the transition: EV ÷ years-1–5 AgEq (7.3 Moz × ~US$52 margin at spot) ≈ 2.8× annual pre-tax margin — cheap on cash flow if the mine is built to plan; P/NAV ~0.7–0.9× at spot (my range) — the highest in the developer set.
Valuation Anchor

~0.7–0.9× a spot NAV, ~3× the FS-deck NAV — priced as a mine under construction, not as a developer waiting for something. That is the correct price for what it is: permitted, funded, building, with a producer's cash flow already inside it. The remaining upside is (a) the gap to ~1.0× NAV as construction milestones land (powerline, portal, mill delivery, commissioning), (b) Los Ricos North being permitted and added to the plan around first pour, and (c) silver — years 1–5 of production at 7.3 Moz AgEq are 60% silver, so a US$85 tape adds ~US$150M of annual margin.

The bear case is not a lost project; it is a US$260–280M capex, a six-month slip, and a stock that trades sideways for eighteen months while the market waits for first pour.

Bucket: quality / jurisdiction premium — with the caveat that the premium is for execution position (permit, cash, contractors), not for Jalisco; this is the Osisko Metals archetype from the copper file, and the first developer in this file the market pays up for.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~6%. CEO Brad Langille ~16.0M shares / ~3.7% (~C$70M) — a founder-era holding built through purchases, option exercises and equity compensation over fifteen years; plus ~2.5M options and DSUs. COO Nehme ~1.1%; directors Gaunce 0.5%, Turner 0.3%, Jessome 0.3%. CEO pay ~US$1.2–1.5M/yr, ~90% equity. 8.9M options at C$1.15–3.25.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Quiet — grants, not trades. Option grants Dec 2025 (Langille, Hatfield, Nehme, Turner); Langille received 85k RSU/DSU shares (Dec 26); director Cooper exercised and sold ~140k in Aug 2026. No open-market buying and no meaningful selling by the CEO through a 2× move. Governance note: directors Turner and Cooper drew 21–27% withhold votes at the March 2026 AGM; Chair Turner's law firm (Fasken) is company counsel; Aguirre resigned Jun 2026.
Strategic & prominent
No 10%+ holder; no strategic miner; no named financier. Institutions ~30%: Global X (SIL) 3.7%, Franklin Templeton 3.3%, Van Eck (GDXJ) 3.1%, Konwave 2.8%, ASA 2.2%, Sprott Gold Equity Fund ~2%, Amplify (SILJ), Goehring & Rozencwajg. Eric Sprott: no disclosed position. Rick Rule interviews Langille at his symposium but holds nothing disclosed. Palisades, Crescat: none.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~30%, insiders ~6%, retail ~64%. 433.5M shares; FD 475.1M (27.1M in-the-money warrants @ C$3.50 = ~US$67M if exercised). Halifax HQ; ~225 Mexican employees.

Read: A founder-CEO with a real, long-held stake who has neither bought nor sold through a doubling; no famous names, no strategic, an ETF-and-fund register. Nobody outside is signalling anything; the insider signal is simply that the man who has built three Mexican mines still owns 3.7% of the fourth. The weak spot is board governance (withhold votes, counsel as chair), not alignment.

Jurisdiction risk

National: Mexico's permitting freeze — survived, at a cost of two years. The 2023 mining-law reform stands (upheld by the Supreme Court, Jun 2025), Sheinbaum has confirmed no new concessions, the implementing regulation is still unpublished, and SEMARNAT's backlog (176 MIAs inherited in 2024) is being cleared at 12–15 months per file — GoGold's June 2026 approval is part of that clearance. It was underground-first by design, to sidestep the open-pit controversy.

Local: manageable but not benign. Hostotipaquillo is in Jalisco, CJNG's home state; the February 2026 killing of "El Mencho" at Tapalpa set off roadblocks across the state and a succession fight; no incident at Los Ricos is reported. Surface rights via Ejido Cinco Minas (2020 agreement, 12+12 years, escalating payments to US$100k/yr in production) and private landholders for the mill site; US$20M of local purchasing in 2025. The August 2026 eleven-day ejido blockade at Endeavour's Terronera, also in Jalisco, is the template for what local friction looks like here. Water via a CONAGUA concession "available at a cost"; power from CFE's La Yesca hydro over a 36 km line.

Jalisco is not Sinaloa — but it is the state where the cartel's leadership war is being fought this year.

Differentiator
  1. Every gate the other silver developers still face is behind it: permit received, capex funded from cash, no debt, no stream, no royalty, construction started, contractors on site.
  2. A producer inside a developer — Parral has funded the company for a decade and still generates ~US$25M+ a year, so the build carries no financing risk and the equity has already absorbed its dilution.
  3. Grade — 145 g/t Ag and 1.39 g/t Au in reserve, with a 3,034 g/t AgEq geotech hit below the stopes; AISC US$11–12/oz AgEq puts it in the lowest-cost decile.
  4. A team that has done this three times in Mexico — Langille built Ocampo and El Cubo at Gammon Gold and Parral in 18 months; the COO ran Ocampo's construction.
  5. A second permitted-in-waiting project, Los Ricos North, larger than the first.

Read it honestly: everything that makes it safe is why it trades at 3× the FS-deck NAV. The market has paid for the permit and the money; it has not yet paid for the mine.

Exploration upside

Near-mine, high impact on sequencing · moves the needle: medium. The Eagle zone (21 m @ 3,034 g/t AgEq, 250 m below the FS stopes) could pull very high grades into the early years; the FS resource is otherwise well defined. Los Ricos North's 110 Moz AgEq PEA is the real expansion — a permit application is planned around first pour, with a revised PEA/PFS that was promised for 2025 and has not appeared. Exploration is not the thesis; construction is.

The promised Los Ricos North study update is a year late — a small tell about bandwidth during the build.

Next Catalyst

Construction milestones: powerline (Nov 2026), portal / ramp / paste plant (Jan 2027), SAG mill delivery (May 2027), commissioning (Jan 2028), first pour Q2 2028; quarterly Parral production and FY results (Dec); Los Ricos North permit application (~Q1 2027) and study update; any capex re-statement; Jalisco security.

Open Questions
  • What is the real capex in 2026 dollars — US$227M, or the ~US$260M that circulates — and when does the company say so?
  • Which permits exactly are in hand: MIA, land-use change, explosives, water — and are any conditional?
  • How does the underground plan handle the old Cinco Minas workings, and what is the contingency if ground conditions differ?
  • Does Parral's AISC keep rising toward US$40+, and does it matter once construction cash is committed?
  • What is the security plan for a 150–500-person site in Hostotipaquillo through a cartel succession?
  • At ~0.8× spot NAV, what is left to earn before first pour — and is Los Ricos North the answer?

Track record
  • Langille co-founded Gammon Lake/Gammon Gold; built Ocampo (Mexico) to production ~2006–07 and acquired Mexgold/El Cubo; left 2007 as Ocampo ramp-up disappointed and an ~$80M class action over stock-option handling was filed against Gammon (2007–08) — a build that worked technically but a rough shareholder episode in the 2006–08 cycle (https://www.northernminer.com/regulatory-issues/gammon-gold-sees-class-action-claim/1000219100/; https://gogoldresources.com/corporate/management)
  • Nayarit Gold (advisor 2007–10) merged into Capital Gold in 2010, which was then bought by Gammon/AuRico in 2011 — small exitsource
  • GoGold: Parral tailings operation built 2014 and still producing cash (US$31M revenue Q1 FY26) — an operating hitsource
  • GoGold sold Santa Gertrudis to Agnico Eagle for US$80M, Sep 2017 — a clean exit in a mid-cyclesource
  • Los Ricos: discovered/acquired 2019, FS Feb 2025 (US$227M capex, NPV US$355M), permit June 2026, construction started Aug 2026 with US$284M cash and no debtsource
  • Equity raised to fund it: C$75M Apr 2025, C$86.25M Jun 2025, C$144M Apr 2026 (https://resourceworld.com/gogold-raises-75-million-for-los-ricos-silver-project-mexico/; https://www.fasken.com/en/experience/2026/04/go-gold-resources-inc-completes-144-million-bought-deal-financing)

Boards today: Langille: 1 public board (GoGold). Turner: 2 (GoGold chair, Arcadium Lithium) plus full-time law practice.

Fit to this job
Closest fit in this batch: Langille and COO Nehme built and ran Ocampo and El Cubo in Mexico, and the same team built Parral and has operated it since 2014. Los Ricos South is an underground silver-gold mine in Jalisco — same country, same team, same contractors culture. New for them: an underground mine of this scale (first pour targeted June 2028) and scaling from a small tailings reprocessor to a mid-tier producer; Ocampo's ramp-up history is the cautionary precedent.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Langille controls ~16.0M shares directly/indirectly (incl. 10.9M via Grupo Pan American and 4.5M by spouse) — ~3.7% of ~430M shares, worth ~US$46M; D&O group 6.4% per Mar 2024 circular. Mix of founder/early shares and awards; no recent open-market buying found (not verified either way). CEO total comp US$1.48M FY2023 (salary US$134k, bonus US$497k, share/option awards US$564k, consulting fees ~US$280k via controlled company); Simply Wall St shows ~US$1.2M latest year. Reasonable at today's ~US$1.2B market cap, high relative to the C$384M cap it was paid at. Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

  • Gammon Gold class action (2007) during Langille's tenure — historical, not GoGold
  • CEO pay US$1.2–1.5M with ~90% in bonus/equity, partly paid as consulting fees via a Langille-controlled company

Gate Getting La Preciosa's economics onto paper — and then delivering them. Funded to the next catalyst Fully funded. A standalone La Preciosa mill (uncosted) would be financed from cash and cash flow; no raise contemplated. The open question is capital allocation, not capital availability.
Thesis

A 20-year-old Durango producer (Avino mine: ~2.5 Moz AgEq/yr from a 736 kt/yr mill) using record silver prices to fund the La Preciosa transformation without debt or equity: 100% ownership consolidated in 2025 (royalties and contingent payments bought out), maiden reserve Apr 2026 of 27 Mt @ 145 g/t AgEq for 127 Moz, M&I 301 Moz.

Development ore is already being milled through both Avino circuits (100.7 koz AgEq in Q2, +59% q/q); long-hole sub-level-caving stopes on Level 3 are nearly ready, targeting 500 tpd in H2 2026.

Q2 2026: revenue US$26.8M, EBITDA US$12.6M, net income US$10.9M, operating cash flow US$13.3M on US$68.90 realised silver; cash US$144.2M, working capital US$140.8M, no debt; a 5% buyback running. Stated ambition: a Mexico-focused mid-tier primary silver producer. CEO David Wolfin. Four analyst Buys, consensus target ~US$10.8.

The Gate

Getting La Preciosa's economics onto paper — and then delivering them. There is a reserve but no economic study, no capex, no timeline to steady state: management is still running trade-off studies on hauling ore 15 km to the Avino mill versus building a standalone plant, and said on the Q2 call it needs "more time" before it can message timing. Until that decision is made, the mid-tier story has no NPV and no date.

Sub-gates
  1. Costs — Q2 AISC US$38.75/AgEq oz against 2026 guidance of US$25–27 (cash cost US$28.62 vs US$19–21), driven by silver recovery falling to 69% (from 85% a year earlier; partly oxidised ore from lower-grade Avino areas), near-waste La Preciosa development rock put through the mill at high metal prices, less copper (fewer AgEq ounces) and a strong peso — reported silver and gold feed grades actually rose 22% and 30% y/y; gold recovery 72%; H2 must carry ~55–60% of the 2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq guidance.
  2. Mexico — the 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concessions, water permits, no new concessions) matters less for a brownfield with existing concessions, but a standalone La Preciosa plant would need new permits under the Sheinbaum regime.
  3. Silver beta — at ~54% silver revenue and realised prices that doubled y/y, the earnings base is a silver-price call first and an operating story second.

The Q2 print shows the transition cost: EBITDA +69% y/y on price while cost per ounce rose ~50% on poor recovery, near-waste development feed and less copper. That inversion has to resolve when long-hole grades arrive.

Figure used: Q2 2026 AISC US$38.75/oz silver-equivalent, converted to ~US$27.5/oz Ag after gold and copper credits. The US$25–27 guidance (not reaffirmed) would put it at ~31st — the bull case, not the base case, while H1 runs ~50% above it.

Sell-trigger watchLower half to upper half in a year — the cost-curve migration that is a sell trigger, with the fix (long-hole stoping at La Preciosa, sending real ore instead of development rock to the mill) only starting in Q4. Q3 results in November are the first test.

Silver is only ~54% of revenue, so the by-product figure moves ~US$5/oz for every 10% move in gold.

How to read it: picture every primary silver mine in the world lined up from cheapest to most expensive to run (all-in sustaining cost per ounce, weighted by output). The percentile is the share of world output that costs less; the middle line splits the cheaper half from the costlier half. Lower-half mines keep earning when the metal price falls. Dot = 2026, ring = 2025. Silver curve: estimated from 18 primary silver mines' 2026 guidance and H1 actuals (~116 Moz) on the Silver Institute's by-product basis — gold, zinc, lead and copper revenue subtracted; silver-equivalent figures converted (±US$3–5/oz). Approximate — it ranks the names, it is not decimal-precise.
