Valuation Anchor

Valued on cash flow and silver, not on ounces. ~17× annualised Q2 EBITDA, ~10–12× at guided costs; ~US$2.9/oz M&I AgEq.

The re-rate case is arithmetic on volume, not multiple: La Preciosa at 500 tpd of 145 g/t adds ~0.7 Moz AgEq a year (~0.85 Moz contained) — and that is already what the 2026 guide of 2.4–2.7 Moz needs; doubling output needs the undecided standalone mill (~1,500–2,000 tpd), which has no study, capex or date (corrected 2 Oct); if it lands at guided costs and silver holds, EBITDA could double or triple, which is what the analyst targets (~US$10.8) are pricing.

The bear case is the same arithmetic in reverse: silver mean-reverts before the ramp, and you own a US$1B company earning US$50M.

Bucket call: producer / cash flow — the fifth bucket, added for this name; the four developer archetypes don't fit a company with revenue.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~6.4% insiders in aggregate. CEO David Wolfin ~5.17M shares / 3.0% (~US$30M) — a founder-family holding built over three decades (director since 1995), part legacy, part exercised options. COO Carlos Rodriguez ~2.66M / 1.6%. Other directors small, mostly options/RSUs.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Selling, no cash buying. Wolfin sold ~527k shares Oct 2025–Jan 2026 (~C$4.5M, up to C$15.59). Rodriguez sold ~325k Feb–May 2026 (C$9.55–12.40); CFO Nathan Harte 50k @ C$10.83 (Apr); director Michael Clark ~82k; others smaller. The only purchase (Peter Latta, 50k @ C$12.63, Jan 2026) may be an exercise. Net: insiders monetised the 2025 run before the stock halved.
Strategic & prominent
None. No 10%+ holder, no strategic miner, no named financier. The largest holders are silver ETFs: SILJ (Amplify) ~5.2%, SIL (Global X) ~3.6%, Van Eck ~3%, Mackenzie ~3.5%. Sprott a token 0.26M.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~25–32% (101 filers), insiders ~6.4%, retail ~62–69%. ~170M shares; NCIB for 8.4M (5%) approved Apr 2026 — 508k bought in Q2.

Read: The tell here is the direction, not the level: 6% is respectable, but every insider transaction in the last year was a sale, clustered at the top, and the CEO sold ~10% of his stake at C$15 before the stock went to C$8. The buyback is the company buying what its officers sold. The ETF-dominated register means the stock trades with the silver-miner basket regardless of La Preciosa.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the weakest in this file, but brownfield-mitigated. Mexico's 2023 mining-law reform (shorter concession terms, tighter water permits, no new concessions under Sheinbaum, stricter open-pit scrutiny) is the same regime that discounts Oroco in the copper file — but Avino is underground, operating for two decades on existing concessions, and La Preciosa's concessions are held. The exposure is a new standalone mill permit and water, if that route is chosen. Peso strength is a live cost headwind (management cites a 12–15% premium).

Local: low. Durango is an established mining state; La Preciosa was permitted and largely built by Coeur before Avino bought it; no organised opposition known; safety record improving (LTIFR 3.55 in 2025).

Mexico is why a debt-free producer trades at a discount to Canadian peers on EV/oz — and why the discount won't fully close.

Differentiator
  1. A reserve-backed path to doubling — though the step that doubles output (a standalone mill) has no study or capex yet. 127 Moz AgEq P&P at La Preciosa on a company producing ~2.5 Moz AgEq/yr, with US$144M cash, no debt and positive free cash flow — the growth needs no financing, no partner, no stream.
  2. The mill already exists — La Preciosa ore is being processed today through the Avino circuits 15 km away, so the ramp is a mining-rate and grade question, not a construction project (unless the standalone option wins).
  3. 100% ownership, royalties bought out (2025) — every incremental ounce is unencumbered.
  4. Silver leverage with a producer's floor — 54% silver revenue, realised price doubled y/y, and the buyback signals management thinks the equity is cheap.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (an existing mill absorbing La Preciosa ore) is also the source of the Q2 cost blow-out — near-waste development tonnes and oxidised Avino ore pushed silver recovery down to 69% and cost per ounce up, even though reported feed grades rose. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Conversion done; step-outs starting · moves the needle: medium. The 2026 programme (15,000 m at each site) shifted from infill to exploration and step-outs mid-year (6,591 m at La Preciosa by end-Q2), targeting outside the current resource model. With 301 Moz M&I already on the books, more ounces don't change the thesis — grade delivered to the mill does.

The exploration that matters is at the Avino mine itself: sustaining feed grade there while La Preciosa ramps.

Next Catalyst

Q3 2026 production (Oct) and financials (Nov) — first read on long-hole grades and whether AISC turns back toward $25–27; the haul-vs-standalone-mill decision and an economic study / capex for La Preciosa (undated); H2 guidance delivery (needs ~1.3–1.6 Moz AgEq); buyback execution; silver price.

Open Questions
  • What do long-hole stopes actually grade at the mill versus the 145 g/t reserve grade, and when does AISC re-converge with guidance?
  • Haul or build? If standalone, what capex, what permits, and does the US$144M cover it without a raise?
  • Does 2026 guidance (2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq) survive an H1 of ~1.1 Moz?
  • What is the sensitivity of EBITDA to silver at US$50 versus US$70 — i.e. how much of Q2 was price?
  • Does the oxide-tailings project (PFS 2024) ever get a decision, or is it quietly shelved?
  • Why did the stock halve from US$11.99 while silver stayed high — is that a cost story, a silver-momentum unwind, or both?
Context & updates
5 Oct 2026 update

Management candour (review of what was said and when). Flagged early: the Feb 2026 guidance warned costs would be 'higher than recent years', and the Q1 release tied a 16% cash-cost rise to La Preciosa development ore. Played down: Q2 AISC came in ~45–50% above the US$25–27 guide, yet guidance was kept and defended on cost per tonne (where it looks fine) rather than per ounce; the Q2 results release itself gave no explanation for the cost jump and nothing on guidance; the production release led with higher feed grades while silver recovery fell from 85% to 69%. Timelines moved: '500 t/day in H2 2026' became 'nearly complete', then 'we need a bit more time', then a different, bigger and later plan (standalone 2,500–3,000 t/day mill, ~2030) announced on stage on 29 Sep, not in a release. Long-time insiders (~6%) are net sellers. Verdict: not dishonest, but promotional — a yellow flag on the promotional-management sell trigger. Test: do the Q3 reports (Oct/Nov) explain the numbers in the release and revise guidance honestly if H2 falls short, and does the mill plan get a formal announcement?

3 Oct 2026 refresh

Spoken at a 29 Sep conference, not yet in a release: La Preciosa is going to a standalone 2,500–3,000 tpd mill — PFS mid-2027, FS mid-2028, ~16-month build, production ~2030, capex US$100–200M (management estimate), potential 7–8 Moz AgEq a year from La Preciosa. The near-term long-hole start (the old '500 tpd in H2 2026') has slipped to 'Q4, any day now'. Q3 production is due in October.

Q2 2026 (Aug 12)

Revenue US$26.8M (+23%), EBITDA US$12.6M (+69%), net income US$10.9M, OCF US$13.3M; realised silver US$68.90 (+104% y/y); provisional-pricing hit ~US$5M. Cash cost US$28.62 and AISC US$38.75 per AgEq oz vs US$15.11 / US$20.93 a year earlier. Cash US$144.2M, working capital US$140.8M.

534,945 AgEq oz (−17% y/y): 267 koz Ag, 2,178 oz Au, 730 klb Cu on 184 kt milled. La Preciosa 100,658 AgEq oz (+59% q/q); Circuit 2 now on La Preciosa ore; Level 3 stope preparation nearly complete. 508k shares bought back.

2026 outlook (Jan)

2.4–2.7 Moz AgEq; AISC US$25–27; capex US$20–26M; La Preciosa 500 tpd in H2 via long-hole sub-level caving. Production weighted to H2.

  • Wins came in the 2024-26 silver bull cycle; the company diluted through ATMs in the 2015-22 period (unverified detail).

Boards today: Wolfin: Avino (CEO/director) and Silver Wolf Exploration (CEO/director) — 2 public executive roles.

Fit to this job
Exactly the same job: small-scale underground/open-pit silver-gold-copper mining and flotation milling in Durango, which they have done for 13 years. La Preciosa is a second mine 20 km away feeding the same mill — new in scale, not in kind. They have not built a standalone new plant.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Wolfin owns ~3.0% (long-held family position; recent activity is selling, not buying). 2025 total pay ~US$1.43M (20% salary, 80% bonus/equity), +20% y/y, at a ~US$1B company. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/nysemkt-asm/avino-silver-gold-mines/management (circular not fetched).

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Cost blow-out vs guidance (+45% AISC) was left out of the release headline and CEO quote and only explained on the call under questioning.
  • CEO, CFO and COO were all net sellers in the past 12 months (CEO ~US$3.2M, incl. ~210k shares at ~US$8.40 on 23 Jan 2026).
  • CEO also runs a second listed company (Silver Wolf) with properties adjacent to Avino's.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash rose from US$2.7M in December 2023 to US$144.8M in June 2026, mostly from US$98.9M of ATM equity; no bank debt, only US$6–9M of equipment leases.

  3. Shares outstanding rose from 128.7M in December 2023 to 169.9M in June 2026, up 32%; a 5% buyback started in Q2 2026 with US$3.0M repurchased.
  4. Revenue grew from US$43.9M in FY23 to US$92.2M in FY25 and US$66.2M in H1 2026 alone; mine operating margin rose from 18% to 55% as silver doubled.
  5. AISC jumped from US$23.75/oz in FY25 to US$38.75/oz in Q2 26 on fewer payable ounces and a stronger peso; free cash flow was US$20.4M in H1 26.

Partly funded to the next catalyst Sep 28 update: a credit-approved US$850M senior-debt commitment letter (SocGen / KfW IPEX / EDC) — the first binding-grade piece of the stack. It is US$350M short of the US$1.2B mandate, which is the lenders' answer on the gold deck: against US$1,428M of capex, ~US$580M of stream, sub-debt and equity is still to be found (my arithmetic), on a ~US$0.9B company. Funded to the permits; expect the stream and an equity raise to follow definitive documentation, before construction in 2027.
Thesis

Troilus is the former Inmet mine (1996–2010) north of Chibougamau: a 50 MW substation, 60 km of high-voltage line, a permitted tailings facility and an all-weather road already exist. The company (ex-Troilus Gold, renamed Dec 2025) has grown the deposit to P&P 478 Mt @ 0.44 g/t Au = 6.69 Moz Au + 568 Mlb Cu and M&I 10.2 Moz Au. The updated technical report (Sep 8, 2026), on 95,000 hours of basic engineering by BBA: 50,000 tpd open pit, 26-year life, ~251 koz Au + 20 Mlb Cu per year, initial capex US$1,428M (Class 3, +15/−10%), after-tax NPV5% US$3.2B and IRR 22% at US$3,600 Au; AISC US$1,340/oz; construction 2027, first ore Sep 2029, commercial production Mar 2030. Financing is a wall of paper: ECA letters of intent totalling US$1.3B (Euler Hermes US$500M, Finnvera US$300M + US$132M for Metso equipment, EKN US$200M, EDC US$300M), a US$1.2B senior-debt mandate to Société Générale / KfW IPEX / EDC (upsized twice, now a credit-approved US$850M commitment from KfW IPEX and Société Générale, 28 Sep, toward a US$1.1B package with EDC's US$250M pending), offtake MoUs with Aurubis and Boliden, Québec's Filon fast-track selection and a 70 MW Hydro-Québec block granted Jun 2026 — and, until 28 Sep, nothing binding. ESIA filed Jun 2025 to Québec (COMEX) and Canada (IAAC); decisions now guided Q1 2027; the Cree Nation of Mistissini impacts-and-benefits agreement is not yet signed.

Cash ~C$140M (Apr 30), no debt, burn ~C$70M/yr; 554.8M shares after a C$172.5M bought deal at C$1.29 (Nov 2025). CEO Justin Reid (founder; ex-Sulliden). Eight analysts, consensus target ~C$3.80–4.30; stock C$2.16; added to GDXJ Sep 18.

The Gate

Turning the US$850M debt commitment (28 Sep) into a signed US$1.1B facility with EDC's US$250M, and US$3,600 gold into a lender's base case — before the permits, the Cree agreement and the equity gap catch up. The Sep 2026 study tripled the headline NPV entirely through the price deck: at US$2,000 gold the same mine plan is worth US$384M (IRR 7.4%); capex rose 33%, reserve grade fell 0.49 → 0.44 g/t, gold recovery fell 92.7% → 86.7%, AISC rose US$1,109 → US$1,340. Lenders will not underwrite at US$3,600; the debt sizing will be done at a deck where this is a 12–17% IRR project, which is why the mandate was upsized twice before the 28 Sep commitment came in at US$850M, below the US$1.2B mandate.

Sub-gates
  1. The stack — the target structure is 55–65% senior debt, 25–35% stream/sub-debt (US$360–500M, none announced) and ~10% equity (US$140M+, against ~C$140M of cash and C$70M/yr burn).
  2. Permits — federal IAAC and provincial COMEX both in the information-request phase, decisions slipped from "year-end 2026" to Q1 2027.
  3. The Cree IBA — a 2018 pre-development agreement exists; the impacts-and-benefits agreement that a Québec mine cannot open without is still unsigned.
  4. Slippage record — financial close "before end 2025" → Q4 2026; construction decision 2026 → construction start 2027; and the CFO hired in March ran Victoria Gold's finances through the Eagle build.

The 70 MW power block is real and rare. Everything else that matters is a letter, a mandate or a memorandum.

NPV : capex2.2× at US$3,600; ~1.5× at US$3,000; 0.3× at US$2,000.Passes the Rule NPV test only at or above the study deck; IRR 22% base scrapes the bar and fails below US$3,300. The honest read: this is a gold-price call with a 26-year mine attached, and the study says so in its own sensitivity table. Market cap ÷ capex ~0.6× — the thinnest coverage of any funded-in-principle developer here; hence the ~10% equity slice in the target structure.
Valuation Anchor

~0.25× NAV at the US$3,600 deck; ~0.35× at US$3,000; ~2× NAV at US$2,000 — the widest P/NAV range in the file, because the NAV itself swings 10× across plausible gold prices. The re-rate path is the Solaris path: debt close (Q4 2026 guided) → permits (Q1 2027) → IBA → stream and equity → construction 2027 → producer multiple 2030. Developers that complete that sequence in Québec have re-rated from ~0.3× toward 0.7–0.8× NAV — 2.5–3× on progress alone at today's gold, and 4–5× if the market adopts US$4,500+.

The bear case is the sensitivity table: at US$3,000 gold this is a 17% IRR, US$1.4B project that lenders size at half the mandate, and the equity slice becomes US$300–400M on a US$0.8B company.

Bucket: scale & financing — the Solaris archetype: tier-one jurisdiction, huge reserve, technically done, one very large cheque away, and the cheque's size depends on the metal.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~3.4% per filings-based aggregators (19.1M shares); the company factsheet says "management & insiders ~8%", which likely includes 22.5M RSUs and 2.5M DSUs. CEO Justin Reid ~6.3M shares / 1.2% — founder shares (2017) plus RSUs; Catherine Stretch 0.3%. Chair Chantal Lavoie (Dec 2024); Pierre Pettigrew and François Biron among directors. No options outstanding — compensation is RSU-based.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Mixed and small. Reid bought 32,000 @ C$1.87 (Feb 9, 2026); the same week Denis Rivard sold 95,000 @ C$1.82, Jacqueline Leroux 20,000 @ C$2.07, Julien Roufast 7,500. Net: officers trimmed into the post-financing rally; the CEO added modestly. Nothing since the September study.
Strategic & prominent
No confirmed 10%+ holder. Franklin Templeton ~7.4% (40.9M), Van Eck ~5.0% (27.7M — bought 16.5M at C$0.35 in a Feb 2025 private placement, since GDXJ inclusion adds passive weight), CDPQ ~1.9%, Konwave ~2.1%, Tidal ~2.6%. One aggregator shows Equinox Partners 12.9% (68M) — unverified, no early-warning filing found. Investissement Québec (C$11.5M at C$1.10, 2021) and the Fonds FTQ are on the register (current % undisclosed) — provincial capital, which matters for Filon and power. No Eric Sprott, Ruffer or strategic miner.
Institutions / retail
Company: institutions ~64% (~12% Québec-based), retail ~28%, insiders ~8%. Filings-based: institutions ~27%, insiders ~3.4%, public ~69%. 554.8M shares; FD 600.4M; +45% share count in 19 months.

Read: A Québec-institutional register — Franklin, Van Eck, the Caisse, Investissement Québec, the Fonds — which is exactly the shareholder base a US$1.4B Québec build needs and the one that tolerates dilution longest. Management alignment is RSU-based and modest; the CEO's February purchase was small and sincere, the officers' sales small and telling. The unverified 12.9% Equinox Partners line is the one thing to nail down: a committed 13% holder changes the equity-gap arithmetic.

Jurisdiction risk

Provincial / national: as supportive as it gets, with the permits still pending. Québec allocated the full 70 MW Hydro-Québec block in Jun 2026 (two ministers came to site — a real signal in a province where blocks are scarce); Troilus was among the first three projects selected for Filon, the province's strategic-mine fast-track (Jul 2026); Bill 63 (2024) tightened claims and consultation but not for a brownfield with a permitted TSF; federally, Troilus was on the Carney critical-minerals mission to Germany (Aug 2025). ESIA filed Jun 2025 to both levels; COMEX (under the James Bay agreement) and IAAC are in information requests; decisions Q1 2027. Québec's provincial election in Oct 2026 is a continuity question, not a threat.

Local: the Cree relationship is the open item. The Cree Nation of Mistissini signed a pre-development agreement in 2018 and has a joint federal-assessment committee role; the impacts-and-benefits agreement is unsigned. No organised opposition found; Cree members attended the power announcement; the company co-funded cabin rebuilding after the 2023 James Bay fires.

Same province as Osisko Metals; a bigger, longer, more price-geared project — and the IBA is the one licence this file cannot yet check off.

Differentiator
  1. Brownfield scale in Québec: 6.7 Moz of reserves, 26 years, a substation, a transmission line, a permitted TSF and a road — with 70 MW of hydro power already allocated. No other developer in either file has power secured before permits.
  2. The deepest bench of institutional support of any pre-FID name here — four ECAs, three mandated lead arrangers, two European smelters, Investissement Québec and the Fonds FTQ on the register, eight analysts, GDXJ inclusion.
  3. Gold torque with a long fuse — the sensitivity table is the bull case: US$5,000 gold makes this a US$5.5B NPV project against a US$0.8B EV.
  4. A takeout profile — a permitted-in-2027, power-allocated, 250 koz/yr Québec asset is exactly what a mid-tier producer buys (Red Cloud's view), and Agnico's June consolidation of Finland shows what happens to de-risked developers in tier-one belts.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (a huge, long, low-grade, tier-one reserve) is why the capex is US$1.43B and why the IRR is single digits below US$2,500 gold. Scale is the asset and the liability.

Exploration upside

Brownfield, in-pit and underground · moves the needle: low–medium. ~40,000 m in 2026 (24,000 m Z87 pit optimisation, 15,000 m Z87 underground) — 129 m @ 0.95 g/t AuEq incl. 22 m @ 3.38 g/t from an Inferred block inside the reserve pit (Sep 17). Converts Inferred, improves early-year grade, may add an underground phase; does not change the financing arithmetic. At 10.2 Moz M&I the file needs a signed loan, not more ounces.

The Z87 underground work is the one exploration line that could move economics — higher grade into the first decade.

Next Catalyst

Debt financing close (US$850M credit-approved 28 Sep; EDC's US$250M pending; close follows the permits); permits — IAAC and COMEX decisions Q1 2027; Cree IBA (undated); stream / sub-debt and equity package; binding offtakes (Aurubis, Boliden); construction start 2027; first ore Sep 2029. Watch the CFO's first financial-close deadline.

Open Questions
  • At what gold price will Société Générale / KfW / EDC actually size the US$1.2B — and how much of the mandate survives at US$3,000?
  • What does the stream cost: US$360–500M of gold or copper stream on a US$3.2B NPV is a large slice — who provides it and on what deck?
  • When is the Mistissini IBA signed, and what does it cost?
  • Why did like-for-like NPV fall ~55% between the 2024 FS and the 2026 report — is the recovery drop (92.7% → 86.7%) final?
  • How much equity at what price — US$140M is the target; US$300M+ is the scenario if debt is sized conservatively?
  • Is this a mine Troilus builds, or a mine someone buys from Troilus once the permits land?
Context & updates
3 Oct 2026 refresh

No news after the 28 Sep US$850M debt commitment; EDC's US$250M is still subject to final approval, and there is no permit or Cree IBA news. The stock fell 13% in C$ (C$2.16 → C$1.87) with no company news, which lifts the per-share multiples about 15%.

Updated technical report (Sep 8–9, 2026)

After-tax NPV5% US$3.2B / IRR 22% / payback 3.6 yr at US$3,600 Au; capex US$1,428M (+33%); 26-yr LOM; 251 koz Au/yr; AISC US$1,340. Like-for-like at ~US$2,000: NPV US$384M vs US$885M in the 2024 FS. Stock +1.3% on the day.

Financing status (Aug–Sep 2026)

US$1.2B senior-debt mandate (SocGen / KfW IPEX / EDC; upsized from US$700M Mar 2025 → US$1.0B Nov 2025 → US$1.2B May 2026), due diligence "well advanced", credit approval pending, documentation targeted by Dec 31. Finnvera LOI up to US$132M for Metso equipment (Aug 27). ECA LOIs US$1.3B total, all non-binding. No stream, royalty or strategic equity announced.

Power and Filon (Jun–Jul 2026)

Hydro-Québec / MEIE allocated the full 70 MW block (Jun 2); ministers Drainville and Champagne Jourdain at site (Jun 8). Troilus selected for the Filon strategic-project fast-track (Jul 27). Added to GDXJ Sep 18.

Balance sheet (Apr 30, 2026)

Cash + term deposits ~C$140M; no debt; nine-month operating outflow C$55M. Nov 2025 bought deal 133.7M shares @ C$1.29 = C$172.5M, no warrants. A US$35M Auramet bridge at 1%/month was drawn (US$15M) and repaid in 2025 — a liquidity tell before the raise.

Aside

Renamed Troilus Mining Corp. Dec 2025. Ownership data conflict: one aggregator shows Equinox Partners at 12.9% with no early-warning filing found; company factsheet says institutions ~64% incl. ~12% Québec-based. Pierre Pettigrew (ex-federal minister) on the board.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 2/5

Reid financed the project well and disclosed each step, but nobody on the executive has built a billion-dollar mine; the operating bench is a year old.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Justin Reid (President & CEO, director, since Dec 2017): Geologist/MBA; ex-Sprott/Cormark analyst, Paladin Energy EGM, National Bank Financial; President of Sulliden Gold (sold to Rio Alto 2014); MD Aguia Resources 2015–2019 · Chantal Lavoie (Board Chair (non-executive), since Dec 2024): Mining engineer, 35+ yrs; background unverified beyond company statements · Denis Rivard (EVP Projects, since Feb 2025): 35+ yrs leading major mining projects — the build lead · Marty Rendall (CFO, since Mar 2026): 17 yrs CFO Victoria Gold (Eagle mine built 2019; company went into receivership 2024 after heap-leach failure), ex-CFO Electra Battery Materials
Track record
  • Reid: President of Sulliden Gold (Shahuindo, Peru), acquired by Rio Alto Mining in 2014 — a developer exit at the bottom of the cycle; Rio Alto later built Shahuindo (https://troilusgold.com/company/management/; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1407007/000117625614000291/exhibit99-2.htm)
  • Reid: MD of Aguia Resources (Brazil phosphate) 2015–2019 — project not built, no exitsource
  • Reid: Pitchblack Resources shell optioned Troilus from First Quantum in 2017 with a C$23M raise, renamed Troilus Gold; Reid has run it 8+ years from shell to US$1.1B debt commitmentsource
  • Troilus FS May 2024: US$1.074B initial capex; debt mandate grew US$700M (Mar 2025) → US$1.0B (Nov 2025) → US$1.2B (May 2026); US$850M credit-approved commitment from KfW IPEX/SocGen + US$250M EDC proposed, Sep 2026source
  • C$172.5M bought deal Nov 2025 at C$1.29 (incl. over-allotment); share price +432% in 2025 per company (https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/11/05/3181886/0/en/Troilus-Announces-150-Million-Bought-Deal-Public-Offering.html; https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/01/08/3215200/0/en/troilus-delivers-on-key-development-milestones-in-2025-and-enters-a-pivotal-transition-year-in-2026.html)
  • Rendall was CFO of Victoria Gold through the Eagle build and the 2024 heap-leach failure/receivershipsource

Boards today: Reid: Troilus CEO + Delta Resources director (appointed 2023); listed as involved with Cunico Metals (unverified) — 2–3 roles. Lavoie: other boards unverified.

Fit to this job
This is a US$1.07B open-pit redevelopment of a past-producing mine in Quebec — the largest build in this batch. Reid is a capital-markets geologist who has financed developers and sold one (Sulliden) but has never built or operated a mine; the operating bench was only assembled in 2025–26 (Rivard, Rendall, process manager). Jurisdiction fit is good (Quebec, Cree agreements, ECA/EDC backing). New for them: everything about execution — construction, a 50ktpd mill, and servicing US$1.1B of debt. The financing achievement is real but it is the team's first mine.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Insiders ~1.14% (Simply Wall St, 2026); 2019 circular showed insiders buying in private placements, no significant recent open-market purchases found. CEO Reid total comp CA$1.13M last reported year (37% salary, 63% bonus/stock/options). Current circular not fetched (troilusmining.com certificate error). Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/otc-chxm.f/troilus-mining/management; https://resourceworld.com/troilus-gold-insiders-increase-share-ownership/

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Capex grew from the 2020 PEA to US$1.07B in the 2024 FS (scope change to 50ktpd) — unverified exact PEA figure
  • Insider ownership ~1.1%; CEO comp CA$1.13M with 63% in bonus/equity — reasonable at a ~C$700M+ cap, but little bought stock
  • Management bench average tenure 1.8 years — the builders are new to the company
  • New CFO's prior company (Victoria Gold) collapsed in 2024 after a heap-leach failure (he was CFO, not operations)

What the numbers say
  1. Cash C$6.9M (Jul 2024) → C$114.7M at 30 Apr 2026, plus C$25.5M of term deposits (C$140M liquidity) after the C$172.5M bought deal at C$1.29 in Nov 2025. Shares 285M → 553M, +94% in 21 months; ~C$218M raised over the 8 quarters.
  2. Burn has stepped up to ~C$22M a quarter (C$4.8M in Q1 FY25) as the project moves through permitting and engineering: exploration and evaluation spend C$45.5M in 9M FY26 vs C$16.6M a year earlier. Liquidity covers ~19 months before any construction capex.
  3. About 80% of cash goes into the ground. Overhead rose C$5.3M (FY24) → C$8.6M (FY25) → C$11.2M in 9M FY26 but stays at 20–25% of spend; share-based pay C$7.0M in 9M FY26.
  4. The US$15M Auramet bridge loan (May 2025, 12% plus warrants, ~20% effective) cost ~C$2.4M for six months and was repaid in Nov 2025; debt-free since, apart from C$1.7M of leases.
  5. Watch: a going-concern paragraph in the FY25 audit before the raise; FY23 profit came from a C$39.7M non-cash gain on lithium claims sold to Sayona, later sold at a C$14.7M loss; FY26 annual statements (31 Jul) not yet published.

Thesis

AurMac sits 40 km from Mayo on the Silver Trail highway, with a 138 kV line crossing the property and a 69 kV substation on site, next door to Hecla's Keno Hill and the failed Eagle mine. From nothing in 2017 Banyan has drilled >180,000 m and built the May 2026 MRE: Indicated 167.3 Mt @ 0.68 g/t = 3.64 Moz; Inferred 267.2 Mt @ 0.58 g/t = 4.98 Moz — 8.62 Moz, Indicated ounces +60% year-on-year, largely within 200 m of surface and open in every direction. A higher-grade core (0.55 g/t cut-off) holds 2.45 Moz Indicated @ 1.00 g/t. Metallurgy decided the mine type: cyanide leach recovers 90–93% but heap-leach columns only 64–72%, so this will be a mill — CEO Tara Christie talks about 30–40,000 tpd, >250 koz/yr and a 30–40 year life. The maiden PEA (Q4 2026) will be the first capex, strip ratio and NPV anyone has seen; it uses the May resource and excludes all 2026 drilling. The company is drilling 70,000 m in 2026 (up to six rigs; 13.03 g/t over 14.2 m and 5.58 g/t over 21.7 m in new Powerline zones; 1.05 g/t over 52.8 m) and plans 70–100,000 m in 2027. Funding: C$57M cash at Jun 30 plus a C$58M raise at C$2.00 closing ~Sep 29 — Franco-Nevada took C$20M of it, having already bought the 6% NSR over the deposits from Victoria Gold's receiver (C$55M portfolio); Banyan can buy that royalty down to 1% for a one-time C$10M. Alpayana (the Peruvian Gubbins family, owners of Sierra Metals) holds ~8%; Franklin ~7%. Five analysts, targets C$2.50–3.00; stock C$1.98 after +118% YTD and GDXJ inclusion on Sep 21.

Valuation Anchor

US$71 per total ounce, US$168 per Indicated ounce, no study — the market has moved this from a discovery multiple to a pre-PEA developer multiple in eighteen months. The bull case is Snowline: a Yukon bulk-tonnage deposit re-rated 3–4× per ounce once a PEA showed a 25% IRR, and Banyan trades at roughly a quarter of Snowline per ounce today. But Snowline has twice the grade and a PEA in hand; AurMac's 0.62 g/t means its PEA will show a larger mill, a bigger tailings facility and a thinner margin, and a 6% royalty on top until C$10M buys it down.

The re-rate path is PEA (Q4) → royalty buy-down → NND agreement → PFS 2027–28 → a major's cheque; Christie has said openly that 5 Moz+ deposits attract Barrick and Newmont, and Franco-Nevada's equity-plus-royalty position is the kind of endorsement that precedes one.

The bear case is the PEA itself: C$2B of capex, a 15% IRR at US$3,000, and a stock at US$71/oz that has nowhere to go but down until gold does the work.

Bucket: scale & financing, the explorer end of it — the Troilus problem (a huge low-grade reserve whose value is set by the metal price) before the study that would tell us how big the problem is.

Read: A register that outside money likes — a royalty major, a Peruvian operating family, Franklin — and insiders who own little and have been selling into the rise. The Reid sale (C$4M at C$0.80) is the fact I would put to the company; the CEO's C$500k subscription at C$2.00 is the right answer to it, if confirmed. Alignment is thinner than the story.

Jurisdiction risk

Provincial / national: Canada, Yukon — a mining territory rewriting its rulebook. Since the Eagle heap-leach failure (Jun 2024, 20 km away) the Yukon government has committed to all 56 Independent Review Board recommendations, is reviewing every existing quartz mining licence, and is revising the mine-waste-facility guidelines (23 of 56 done by Apr 2026; the rest targeted spring 2027). The IRB concluded heap leaching can proceed with enhanced oversight; Banyan has sidestepped the question by going to a mill — which means a tailings facility, licensed under rules not yet written, in the district where the failure happened. YESAB not yet entered; multi-year once it is. Infrastructure is the genuine asset: all-weather highway, 138 kV line and a 69 kV substation on the property, hydro 40 km away, cell and fibre — though a large mill would need grid expansion the territory has not scheduled.

Local: the weak layer. The First Nation of Na-Cho Nyäk Dun (NND) has no disclosed agreement with Banyan. In August 2025 NND opposed new claims in its territory pending land-use planning (Banyan agreed to stake none); in September 2025 the Chief called the AurMac transfer "concerning" and criticised Banyan's "lack of transparency and communication". The company points to a 50% Yukoner workforce (30% from Mayo), NND Development Corporation contractors, C$3.3M of education funding since 2012 and baseline work since 2021, and has hired an ex-Kaminak sustainability lead and an ex-Alexco environmental manager. NND's MOU with Snowline (Jan 2026; free, prior and informed consent before construction) shows the First Nation is not anti-mining and shows what Banyan does not yet have.

Same territory as Triumph's Freegold — but AurMac has the road, the power line and the resource; what it lacks is the agreement.

Differentiator
  1. Scale with infrastructure: 8.6 Moz — 3.6 Moz Indicated — within 200 m of surface, beside an all-weather highway and under a 138 kV line, 40 km from a hydro dam. No other pre-study name in this file has both the ounces and the access.
  2. A treasury that removes the financing question for two years — ~C$100M pro forma, no debt, no warrants, every raise since 2025 at or above market, drilling expanded 40,000 → 70,000 m rather than cut.
  3. The register — Franco-Nevada holds the royalty and now equity; Alpayana, a Peruvian operating family, took an entire placement; Franklin ~7%; GDXJ inclusion.
  4. A Yukon-native team — Christie founded YESAB's board and ran a placer mine in the territory for a decade; the chair sold Nevsun to Zijin; the corporate-development hire just sold Probe to Fresnillo; John Robins (Kaminak, Great Bear) advises.
  5. Discovery is still running — 13 g/t over 14 m in a new zone, ten undrilled targets, a 720 km² district that is <2% explored.

Read it honestly: the differentiator is quantity and location. The thing that decides the stock — grade against capex — is the one the differentiator says nothing about.

Exploration upside

Very high · moves the needle: high for ounces, low for the PEA. 70,000 m in 2026 with ~25,000 m of assays still to come; 2027 guided at 70–100,000 m at AurMac plus 20–30,000 m regional, starting with the untested Gap zone between Powerline and Airstrip in January. New high-grade zones at Powerline North (13.03 g/t / 14.2 m; 5.58 g/t / 21.7 m; 149 g/t / 0.4 m) could lift the higher-grade core that a mill would mine first. Keno-style silver (10,734 g/t Ag / 1.7 m) and Nitra (5.70 g/t Au + 544 g/t Ag) are district optionality, not thesis. None of this is in the Q4 PEA.

Watch the higher-grade core (0.55 g/t cut-off) more than the headline ounces — a mill's first decade is built from it.

Next Catalyst

Maiden PEA — Q4 2026 (capex, strip, throughput, NPV: the whole re-rate, up or down); C$58M raise closing ~Sep 29; remaining 2026 assays through Dec; royalty buy-down decision (C$10M, undated); 2027 drill start Jan (Gap zone); a resource update on the 2026 drilling (not yet guided); any NND agreement; revised Yukon waste-facility guidelines spring 2027.

Open Questions
  • What capex and strip ratio does the PEA show, and at what throughput — and what is the IRR at US$3,000, not US$3,500?
  • Is the higher-grade core (2.45 Moz @ 1.0 g/t) enough to front-load the mine plan, or does the economics rest on 0.58 g/t Inferred?
  • When is the C$10M royalty buy-down exercised, and why not before the PEA is published?
  • What does an agreement with Na-Cho Nyäk Dun look like, and what has the company done since the Chief's September 2025 statement?
  • How does a 30–40,000 tpd mill get powered — grid expansion timing, LNG bridge cost?
  • Why were directors and the CFO net sellers (Reid C$4.0M) through a year in which the company raised C$135M from outsiders?

3 Oct 2026 refresh

The C$54.3M financing closed 29 Sep (27.16M shares at C$2.00; ~473M shares out, ~505M fully diluted). The company now says proceeds advance AurMac and Nitra 'through 2028'. Maiden PEA still Q4 2026.

C$58M financing and Franco-Nevada (Sep 20–24, 2026)

C$50M brokered LIFE (25M sh @ C$2.00, Canaccord) + C$8M non-brokered (8M @ C$2.00), no warrants, closing ~Sep 29; Franco-Nevada subscribed for 10M shares (C$20M, ~2.1%) on top of the 6% NSR it bought in April. MRE (May 19, 2026) and PEA consultants (Jul 7)

Royalty (Apr 16, 2026)

Franco-Nevada closed the purchase of Victoria Gold's royalty portfolio from the receiver for C$55.0M, including the 6% NSR over the 510 claims covering Powerline and Airstrip and 1% on Banyan's Hyland. Banyan retains the right to buy the 6% down to 1% for a one-time C$10M.

Earn-in and ownership (Sep 2025)

100% of Aurex/McQuesten acquired from Victoria Gold's receiver (C$2.0M + C$1.6M) after Eagle's failure ended Victoria's option; the "strict" 2025 PEA deadline fell away with it. Victoria's 8.6% stake fully sold by the receiver; Alpayana bought essentially all of the Oct 2025 C$31.4M placement at C$0.70 / C$0.97 (FT).

Aside

Five raises in 18 months, all without warrants and each at a higher price (C$0.70 → C$0.97 → C$1.40 → C$1.918 → C$2.00) — an unusually clean dilution record for a Venture explorer. Flow-through spend obligations: C$6.6M by Dec 2026, C$29.7M by Dec 2027 — cash that must go into the ground, not the royalty or the study.

Fit to this job
Stage match is good: AurMac is a large low-grade Yukon oxide/sulphide deposit heading to a maiden PEA, and the team is Yukon-native (Christie grew up in Klondike placer mining; Woloshyn permitted at Keno Hill). Nobody on the executive has taken a hard-rock project through feasibility, permitting (YESAB) and construction; the directors with that experience (Blythe, Halsall-Whitney) are non-executive. New for them: economic studies, Yukon permitting, and the 2024 Victoria Gold/Eagle heap-leach failure makes a Yukon heap-leach PEA a harder sell.

Christie holds ~14.2M shares, 2.6–3.5% depending on source (worth ~C$20M), accumulated via early placements and option exercises (e.g., 500k options at C$0.24 exercised Feb 2025); insiders collectively net sellers of ~C$350k over the trailing year. CEO total comp ~C$627k (53% salary) — in line for a ~C$840M market cap. What the numbers say
  1. Cash was C$57.4M at 30 June 2026 and about C$110M after a C$54.3M placement in September 2026; peak-season burn is C$15.6M a quarter, so about 7 quarters of runway.
  2. Capitalised exploration was C$19.9M in the first nine months of FY26 against C$4.1M of cash G&A, so overhead is about 15% of spend but more than doubled year on year.
  3. Shares outstanding grew from 284.9M in September 2023 to 445.9M in June 2026, up 57%, and about 473M after the September 2026 placement; no debt, streams or royalties sold.
  4. Reported net losses look small only because of non-cash flow-through premium recoveries; the flow-through premium liability was C$16.0M at 30 June 2026.
  5. Every set of statements carries a going-concern note, the auditor changed in August 2025, and C$3.6M was paid to Victoria Gold's receiver to complete 100% of AurMac.

Thesis

The most permit-complete undeveloped gold project in eastern Canada, with cash in the bank and a construction decision weeks away. NexGold (ex-Treasury Metals) bought Signal Gold in Dec 2024 to pair Goliath (Ontario, EA-approved) with Goldboro (Nova Scotia).

Goldboro then collected every major permit in 2025: Crown Land lease (May), ECCC Schedule 2 (Jul), Industrial Approval (Aug), DFO Fisheries Act authorisations (Oct), on top of the Aug 2022 EA — plus a benefits agreement with the Assembly of Nova Scotia Mi'kmaw Chiefs (Dec 2024) now in implementation. Early-works construction began Sep 17, 2026; the updated FS and a board construction decision are both guided to Q4 2026; 26-month build → first gold ~2028; ~100 koz/yr for 11 years.

Goliath's FS was deliberately paused (Jan 2026) to re-optimise while Goldlund gets 25,000 m of infill — sequenced, not abandoned; sell-side models Goliath lifting group output above 200 koz/yr by ~2032. CEO Kevin Bullock; COO Jeremy Wyeth (De Beers / Anglo mine-building). Sell-side: NBF Buy C$5.50, Red Cloud Buy C$4.30.

The Gate

The Q4 2026 double reveal: updated capex and the financing package to fund it. Every NPV quoted for Goldboro is built on 2021 costs and US$1,600 gold; the updated FS will almost certainly show a much higher NPV and a much higher capex (industry re-baselining since 2022 has run +30–60%). If capex lands near C$400M+, the C$101M treasury covers only a quarter of it, and the plan leans on the non-binding US$175M Appian credit LOI plus whatever equity or stream fills the gap — on a company that has already sold a 2.9% NSR to Appian (US$24M) until 1.25 Moz.

Sub-gates
  1. Goliath is on hold — the "two-mine, 200 koz" story is now one mine plus a study-in-waiting.
  2. Nova Scotia execution — first hard-rock gold mine built in the province in decades, 350-person construction camp, contractor and labour market untested at this scale.
  3. Sprott Streaming obligations on Goliath (share issuances under the amended 2022 agreement) sit on top.

Watch whether the construction decision is unconditional or "subject to financing."

Valuation Anchor

~US$75–100/oz on reserves (EV ~C$250–330M ÷ ~2.4 Moz AuEq P&P) and ~US$40–50/oz on 4.7 Moz M&I — for permitted ounces in Canada that is the cheap end of the developer range. P/NAV is unknowable until the FS reset: on the stale studies, market cap ≈ 0.6× combined NPV5% (C$664M); on a spot-price deck the market cap is likely a fraction of combined NPV, which is the bull case NBF/Red Cloud are pricing.

Bucket: cheap defined ounces — reserves, permits and a study exist, so it qualifies; the discount is one variable (capex/financing), legible in the same way Los Andes's permitting discount is. Emperor is the mirror image: ounces everywhere, nothing defined.

Modest cash buying, some option selling. Insiders took 287,500 units + 178,000 FT shares in the Oct 2025 bought deal (Bowering, Baranowsky, Bullock, McNeill, Lekstrom). Lekstrom bought in the market five times Oct 2025–Mar 2026 (C$1.32–2.08); Baranowsky twice; new director David Anthony 30k @ C$1.33 (Jun 2026). Against that: Baranowsky exercised-and-sold 59k, Lekstrom 26k, plus two un-named exercise/sales. Net: directors buy small, executives take some off.
Strategic & prominent
Frank Giustra (Fiore) ~5% — strategic advisor since Jul 2024, bought in cash (4.75M shares + 2.65M warrants then; "meaningful" participation in the Nov 2024 financing), plus a share of 1.5M advisor options @ C$1.00. Sprott Asset Management ~3.9% (was 11.4% in Nov 2024, diluted by the Signal merger and 2025 raises — not sold). Institutions / retail
Company deck: institutions 61%, retail 32%, Giustra 5%, management 2%. Named: Ninepoint ~3.1%, Extract Advisors ~3.1% (former lender), EdgePoint ~2.7%, Middlefield, IG, Mackenzie. No 10%+ holder. 257.7M shares; 98.8M warrants (avg C$1.68) → FD 364M.

Read: Institutional register with one famous name. Giustra's 5% was bought with cash and he has stayed through the merger — that is the vote of confidence. Management's 2% is mostly paper (RSUs/options), which for a C$400M company about to make a construction decision is thin: the board has more skin than the CEO. The 98.8M warrants are the quiet dilution.

Jurisdiction risk

National / provincial: done. Federal (ECCC Schedule 2, DFO), provincial (EA 2022, Industrial Approval, Crown Land lease, mining lease) and Indigenous (ANSMC Mutual Benefits Agreement, implementation committee meeting through 2026) — the gate that dominates most developers is simply not here.

Local: low. Rural Guysborough County, an historic gold district; Nova Scotia has an anti-mining current (the 2024–25 uranium and fracking debates), but Goldboro is through it and the province granted the lease. Goliath: Ontario EA approved; First Nations engagement ongoing.

Permits done is why the easy re-rate has already happened (+155% in 2025).

Differentiator
  1. Permits done + cash on hand — the one combination almost no gold developer has.
  2. 2.26 g/t open-pit reserve grade — roughly double the typical Canadian open-pit developer, which is what makes a ~C$271M-class build plausible at all.
  3. C$101M, no debt, and an Appian relationship that has already put money in.
  4. A second permitted platform (Goliath, EA-approved) that a producer could bolt on — this is what a mid-tier acquirer buys.

Read it honestly: "permitted and funded to a decision" is also why the remaining upside is the capex-vs-price arithmetic in the updated FS, and that cuts both ways.

Exploration upside

Conversion, not discovery · moves the needle: low–medium. Goldboro RC infill: 61.22 g/t over 12 m in the early-mining area (Aug 2026); Goldlund 2026 infill: 15.21 g/t over 20.1 m, 5.11 g/t over 21.8 m, 9.30 g/t over 11 m. These matter for the updated MRE grade and the starter-pit sequence, not for size. Airborne EM and gravity surveys over 32,000 ha at Goldboro (interpretation ongoing) are the only genuine step-out lever.

At 4.7 Moz M&I the file needs economics more than ounces.

Entry plan · €1,000 as an illustration
Step 0 · waitingNothing bought. Two alerts set: the updated Feasibility Study (guided Q4 2026) and a price alert at C$1.15. Plan written 25 Sep 2026 at ~C$1.40. The €1,000 is illustrative (≈ C$1,500 ≈ ~1,050 shares) — the point is the 40/60 split and the events, not the amount; scale it.

A decision tree tied to events, not dates, worked through for an example position of €1,000. Two entries only — with a small position, three tranches at a German broker would cost 3–5% in fees. Not advice; my read of the situation written down in advance so that on the day I read numbers against thresholds I set beforehand, not against the price move.

Step 1the Feasibility Study (Q4 2026, most likely Nov–Dec): read three numbers and one sentence before doing anything
WhatGreenRed
Initial capex≤ C$400M> C$450M

After-tax IRR at a ≤ US$3,000 gold deck≥ 25%< 18%
The construction-decision sentence"Board has approved construction""subject to financing" / "decision deferred"

Three or four green → project intact; any dip afterwards is a discount. Two or more red → the project got worse, not cheaper. Stop. Do not buy the dip. Re-run the card first.

Step 2first tranche: €400 (~40%)
  1. Mostly green and the stock falls ≥ 12% on FS day or within the following week → buy €400 in the market. The discount is driven by the size of the cheque, not by the project.
  2. Mostly green and the stock rises → buy €400 anyway within a week. The dip is not coming; an unconditional decision is worth more than the 15% saved. Don't chase beyond +20%.
  3. Red → nothing.
Step 3second tranche: €600 (~60%) — on the financing announcement (4–12 weeks after the FS, most likely Q1 2027)

This is the real entry. Buy in the market on the day the bought deal is announced or the next morning, at or near the deal price — the institutions' price without the four-month hold. Read the deal first:

  1. Go (€600): equity ≤ C$120M, a stream ≤ US$100M, the Appian debt binding — total dilution under ~40%. A strategic (a producer) taking a stake at a premium is the best possible signal: buy that day regardless of price.
  2. Caution (€300): equity C$120–200M with no stream and no strategic — dilution 50–75%. Probably still fine, the project is funded, but the re-rate is slower.
  3. No-go (keep the €600): a bridge or a small raise "to advance detailed engineering" without a full package — they couldn't get the money.
Step 4no financing announced by end-March 2027

They are waiting for the stock to recover so the C$1.68 warrants fund it. Buy the €600 anyway in two €300 pieces, April and June. The overhang is a grind, not a cliff; waiting longer only costs the re-rate.

Step 5once in: sell-or-hold triggers
  1. Sell if the construction decision is withdrawn or the project is put "under review".
  2. Sell half if the stock doubles before first gold (2028) — construction stocks re-rate fastest between financing and commissioning; a double on a pre-production developer is worth banking half of.
  3. Otherwise hold to first gold. The thesis is a permitted mine reaching production; don't trade the quarters in between.
PracticalWhere to buy, and the most likely outcome

Main liquidity is TSXV: NEXG; OTCQX: NXGCF; Frankfurt: TRC1 is thin — use TSXV access if the broker offers it and accept the CAD conversion. Most likely single outcome: the FS is fine (capex ~C$400M, decision conditional) and the stock drifts 10–15% lower over two months without a dramatic dip. The plan still works; the average entry is ~C$1.25 rather than C$1.05, and the money was never in the timing — it is in whether the mine gets built.

Plan log: 25 Sep 2026 — plan written at ~C$1.40; Step 0, nothing bought. 26 Sep — marked as pick (💸) in tracker and rankings. 1 Oct — Sep 17 release: early-works construction started at Goldboro ahead of the FS; Sep 23: strong Goldlund infill (14.07 g/t / 7 m). Still Step 0 — the FS thresholds are the trigger, and spending before the decision suggests management expects to pass them.

A high-grade Colombian underground mine that has been "about to" reach commercial production for a year, freshly de-levered by doubling its share count, with the cash from its latest raise sent to a copper explorer

Gate Turning 43 tpd of hand-mined ore into an 834 tpd mechanised mine — on time, on grade, in Titiribí. The PEA's 558% IRR is an artefact of counting only the US$11M of capex not yet spent; what it really says is that the entire value sits in execution: a new portal and 600 m ramp (funded by June's Trafigura upsizing), a plant that has slipped from Q3 to Q4 2026, and a resource that is 79% Inferred and has never been mined at scale. Sub-gates: (1) security — Suroeste Antioquia had a record 320 homicides in 2025; Titiribí itself had six in Q1 2026 after a February massacre (one in all of 2025), and El Colombiano flags new mining projects as extortion targets; (2) capital allocation — the last C$28.8M of equity was redeployed into a copper explorer rather than Zancudo, while Zancudo's own development is funded by an offtaker's prepayment; (3) costs — cash cost US$2,513/oz in the artisanal phase against a PEA LOM US$2,448 that assumes mechanised mining; silver payability 20–45% on raw ore; (4) a slipping Spanish leg — Aguablanca has moved three times, its US$20M note raised US$7.5M, Lomero's PEA never came.

Thesis

Zancudo, in Titiribí (Antioquia), is a historic high-grade gold-silver district (worked since the 1700s) that Denarius — an Iacono / ex-Gran Colombia Gold vehicle — is bringing back as a 1,000 tpd underground flotation operation. Early production since Q2 2025 by hand-mining accessible workings and shipping raw ore to Trafigura: H1 2026 6,244 t at 11.4 g/t Au / 237 g/t Ag for 1,563 oz Au + 17.5 koz Ag payable, revenue US$8.4M, gross margin ~40%. The PEA (Mar 2026) shows after-tax NPV5% US$324M, 11-year life at 834 tpd, 465 koz Au + 2.2 Moz Ag payable, AISC US$2,482/oz — on only US$11M of remaining capex because the plant is already under construction; first concentrate is now guided Q4 2026.

On Jul 31, 2026 the company retired C$34.2M of 12% gold-linked convertible debentures (Iacono and Aris Mining were the large holders) by issuing 223.6M shares — share count 213M → 437M — eliminating a US$38.8M working-capital deficit and ~C$157M of future gold-premium obligations.

Three weeks later Trafigura bought 67M units at C$0.43 (C$28.8M; now 14.8%) and the proceeds went, in full, into a 15.3% stake in Copper Giant Resources (the copper file's Mocoa).

Spain: 21.8% of Aguablanca (Ni-Cu, restart slipped to mid-2027, non-recourse financing half-placed), 100% of Lomero (1.9% CuEq Indicated, PEA never delivered) and Toral (maiden 14.8 Mt Inferred Zn-Pb-Ag, Sep 2026). Cash US$18.9M at Jun 30; Trafigura prepay US$16M facility (US$7M undrawn).

The Gate

Turning 43 tpd of hand-mined ore into an 834 tpd mechanised mine — on time, on grade, in Titiribí. The PEA's 558% IRR is an artefact of counting only the US$11M of capex not yet spent; what it really says is that the entire value sits in execution: a new portal and 600 m ramp (funded by June's Trafigura upsizing), a plant that has slipped from Q3 to Q4 2026, and a resource that is 79% Inferred and has never been mined at scale.

Sub-gates
  1. Security — Suroeste Antioquia had a record 320 homicides in 2025; Titiribí itself had six in Q1 2026 after a February massacre (one in all of 2025), and El Colombiano flags new mining projects as extortion targets.
  2. Capital allocation — the last C$28.8M of equity was redeployed into a copper explorer rather than Zancudo, while Zancudo's own development is funded by an offtaker's prepayment.
  3. Costs — cash cost US$2,513/oz in the artisanal phase against a PEA LOM US$2,448 that assumes mechanised mining; silver payability 20–45% on raw ore.
  4. A slipping Spanish leg — Aguablanca has moved three times, its US$20M note raised US$7.5M, Lomero's PEA never came.

The debenture conversion fixed the balance sheet; it did not fix the mine. Q4's first concentrate is the first hard data point on whether the PEA is a plan or a spreadsheet.

Valuation Anchor

~0.7× PEA NAV on a 79%-Inferred resource, ~US$1,000/oz Indicated — priced as if the ramp is done. At 834 tpd and ~40 koz/yr the PEA's mid-life years earn ~US$60M of margin at US$4,000; 8–10× that is US$500–600M, which is the analyst target and the bull case.

The bear case: it never reaches 834 tpd, costs stay at US$2,500 in a security-compromised district, and the 573M fully-diluted shares make every further raise a heavier lift. The Spanish portfolio and the Copper Giant stake are real but currently consume attention and capital rather than provide it.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — high grade, no reserves, execution-priced; it does not qualify for cheap defined ounces (Inferred-dominated) and does not yet qualify as a producer (US$8M of H1 revenue, negative operating cash flow).

Shareholder structure
Management & board
Serafino Iacono (Exec Chairman) ~16.0% (80.8M shares after the Trafigura placement; 18.5% at Jul 31) plus 2.44M options and 8.7M warrants. How he got there matters: ~27.6M shares were bought with cash over 2023–25 (market purchases at ~C$0.54, placements at C$0.50 in Mar and Nov 2025, warrant exercises) — then +53.2M shares on Jul 31, 2026 in settlement of C$8.5M of debentures he held (15.2M on conversion, ~37.9M as make-whole for future gold premiums at the NPV price of C$0.81). CEO Restrepo-Solano ~4.75M pro forma; CFO Davies ~0.7M; other directors not disclosed online (circular on SEDAR+ only). 13.7M options outstanding.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Iacono buying with cash, CFO selling. Iacono: 1.85M placement units @ C$0.50 (Nov 2025), 260k in the market @ ~C$0.79 (May 19, 2026), 219k @ ~C$0.60 (Jul 10, 2026, three weeks before the conversion) — consistent, small, and at the lows. CFO Davies exercised 249k options and sold 200k @ ~C$0.83 (Feb 2026, a third of his holding). The July 31 settlement dwarfs all of it.
Strategic & prominent
Trafigura 14.8% (74.6M + 19.2M warrants; 17.9% partially diluted) — offtaker, prepay lender and now the second-largest holder after the Aug 2026 C$28.8M placement at C$0.43; also holds 20% of the Copper Giant offtake. Aris Mining ~11.8% (59.6M; 13.6% at Jul 31) — the Iacono/Giustra-founded producer, holder since the Zancudo vend-in; bought 4M units @ C$0.50 (Nov 2025) and received 36.5M in the debenture settlement; "for investment purposes only." Ruffer LLP ~4.8% (24.0M) — the one notable outside institution, origin undisclosed. Aton Ventures ~2.6% (was 12.2% in Mar 2025, diluted). Frank Giustra is not a disclosed Denarius holder — his link is through Aris and as a co-investor in Copper Giant.
Institutions / retail
Iacono + Trafigura + Aris ≈ 42–43% in three aligned hands; Ruffer ~5%; the rest retail. No formal shareholder agreement disclosed. 504.1M shares; 67.4M warrants + 13.7M options → FD ~585M. AGM turnout 62% (Jun 2026).

Read: The highest insider ownership in the file, and the most ambiguous. Iacono has ~US$37M in the stock and has kept buying with cash at the lows — that is real alignment. But two-thirds of his position arrived on Jul 31 in a settlement he negotiated as a debenture holder, at an effective ~C$0.15, approved by a minority vote; and the three largest holders — chairman, offtaker-lender, affiliated miner — are one network controlling ~42%. High ownership here is as much control as conviction. Read it as: the insiders will not let it fail, and the insiders will decide who gets diluted when it needs money.

Jurisdiction risk

National: turned favourable, unproven. Abelardo de la Espriella won the Jun 21, 2026 runoff (49.7% vs 48.7%), inaugurated Aug 7; Mines minister María Nohemí Arboleda; stated agenda of faster permitting, formalising legal mining and reopening exploration, driven by a 6.4%-of-GDP deficit — the same reframing the copper file applied to Copper Giant. Zancudo's environmental licence (2024) and industrial permit (Oct 2025) are in hand.

Local: the live risk is security, not licence. Suroeste Antioquia: record 320 homicides in 2025, 81 in Q1 2026 (18.6% of the department), Clan del Golfo offshoots and Medellín groups contesting; Titiribí six homicides in Q1 2026 after a Feb 25 massacre. No community opposition or informal-miner conflict found — but a 1,000 tpd operation in a district worked by hand for 250 years is an extortion and invasion target by construction. Board includes a former Procuradora General (Margarita Cabello) — a political-risk hire.

Same national tailwind as Copper Giant; a worse local layer, and Denarius now owns 15% of Copper Giant, so the Colombia exposure is doubled.

Differentiator
  1. Grade, a built plant, and a trading house inside the tent. 6.9 g/t Indicated / 5.6 g/t Inferred with 11 g/t coming out of the hand-mined phase is top-decile for an underground gold developer, and the plant, licence and portal are funded and largely built — the PEA's US$11M residual is real in that narrow sense.
  2. Trafigura as offtaker, US$16M prepay lender and ~15% shareholder — an aligned counterparty that has doubled down twice in 2026.
  3. A clean balance sheet for the first time — no debentures, no gold-premium overhang, US$18.9M cash.
  4. Optionality in three other assets and a listed copper stake, all carried at little inside a US$225M EV.

Read it honestly: the differentiators — Trafigura's embrace and the Iacono/Aris network — are also the concentration and related-party risk: three affiliated holders own ~42%, the offtaker is the lender is the shareholder, and the debenture make-whole (146M shares at an NPV of future gold premiums) went largely to insiders. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, in-mine · moves the needle: medium–high. The thesis needs Inferred → Indicated more than new ounces: 79% of the PEA's material is Inferred. The 2026 programme (15,100 m, 3,200 m brownfield) is producing high-grade intercepts (33 m @ 5.68 g/t; 1 m @ 41.8 g/t) at Las Brisas — good for the grade narrative, not yet a category upgrade. Toral (Sep 2026 maiden) and Lomero add tonnes in Spain that the market gives no credit for and won't until a study exists.

An updated Zancudo MRE with a meaningful Indicated share would do more for the stock than any hole.

Next Catalyst

First concentrate from the 1,000 tpd plant (Q4 2026) — already slipped once; Q3 production (late Oct) and Q3 financials (~Nov 13); new portal / 600 m ramp progress; Aguablanca US$25M facility (guided end-Q3 — check) and the mid-2027 restart; an updated Zancudo MRE; Copper Giant's PEA (Q4 2026) as a mark on the C$28.8M stake; the Toral West option.

Open Questions
  • What does the plant actually run at in its first two quarters — and what grade, when mechanised stopes replace hand-picked ore at 11 g/t?
  • How much of the 832 koz Inferred converts, and what does the PEA look like on Indicated-only material?
  • Why send C$28.8M of fresh equity into Copper Giant while Zancudo's ramp is funded by an offtaker's prepay — strategy, or Iacono-network capital recycling?
  • What is the security plan for a mechanised operation in Titiribí after the Feb 2026 massacre, and who bears the cost?
  • Does Aguablanca ever restart on Denarius's balance sheet, or does the 21.8% get sold?
  • With 573M shares fully diluted, what is the next raise — and at what price?
Context & updates
6 Oct 2026 update

Listed as a developer although it already sells ore. Zancudo ore goes directly to Trafigura (~US$8.6M revenue in H1 2026; Q2 ~43 t/day and ~970 oz payable gold), far below the 500–1,000 t/day plan. The value still rests on commissioning the plant (due Q3/Q4 2026) and restarting Aguablanca (mid-2027), which are developer milestones — so it is tagged 'early ore sales' and stays on the developer list. Rule: it moves to the producer list once the plant runs near design capacity and covers its own operating costs for two quarters in a row; checked every Saturday.

3 Oct 2026 refresh

No release since 9 Sep. First concentrate from the 1,000 tpd plant is still guided Q4. The Aguablanca US$25M facility, guided for end-Q3, has not been announced (missed). The stock fell 15% to C$0.56 with no news, which lifts the per-share multiples ~18%.

Debenture retirement (Jul 31, 2026)

C$34.2M of 12% gold-linked convertibles (Series 1 C$19.9M @ C$0.45; Series 2 C$14.3M @ C$0.60) retired for 223.6M shares: 67.9M on conversion + 146.5M make-whole (NPV of future gold premiums, settled at C$0.81 VWAP) + fees. Iacono 18.5%, Aris Mining 13.6% post-deal. ISS/Glass Lewis supported; ~C$157M of future obligations avoided; working capital swings from −US$38.8M to +US$12.8M pro forma.

67M units at C$0.43 (C$28.81M) with C$0.60 warrants to 2029; Trafigura 14.8%. Same day: 40.0M Copper Giant shares at C$0.72 (C$28.8M) = 15.3%; CEO Restrepo-Solano joins CGNT advisory board. Prepay facility upsized to US$16M (Jun 18).

3,907 t shipped (+67% q/q) at 11.3 g/t Au / 217 g/t Ag; 970 oz Au + 9.7 koz Ag payable; revenue US$4.9M; gross profit US$1.9M; cash cost US$2,513/oz; net income +US$8.3M on a US$15.5M non-cash debenture gain. Cash US$18.9M. Plant first concentrate re-guided to Q4.

Management review
Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 4/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 5/5

Iacono has built a Colombian underground producer before (Segovia) and owns 16% with real market buying: a team that has done this job. Held at B, not higher, because every Denarius date since 2024 slipped by a year or more and each slip was reported as a fresh target. Candour stays 2 — watch the plant commissioning date.

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

Track record
  • Bolivar Gold (co-founder): sold to Gold Fields in 2006 — a 2003-07 cycle win; price not verified this sessionsource
  • Pacific Rubiales/Pacific Exploration & Production (co-chairman): Colombia's largest independent oil producer, restructured under creditor protection in 2016 wiping out equity — the big miss; not verified via fetch this sessionsource
  • Gran Colombia Gold (executive chairman): built Segovia into a profitable underground gold producer after a debt restructuring; became Aris Mining in 2022; Aris now holds 11.8% of Denariussource
  • Denarius Zancudo: Feb 2024 release said production in 2024 'remains on track', plant operational Dec 2024; mining actually started March 2025 and the plant is now guided for Q3/Q4 2026 — ~2 years late (https://www.newsfilecorp.com/release/199750/ ; https://denariusmetals.com/denarius-metals-announces-start-of-mining-operatio-10014/ ; https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/denarius-metals-announces-second-quarter-and-first-half-2026-production-results-its)
  • Aguablanca (Spain, 50%): restart 'within one year of dewatering' (Feb 2024), 'within next 12 months' (Mar 2025), now mid-2027 target; US$20M notes offering by Rio Narcea launched; US$25M facility unconfirmed as of Sept 2026source
  • Capital structure: C$34.2M convertible debentures (C$0.45 and C$0.60 conversion) plus 189M shares; C$16.7M from warrant exercises early 2026source

Boards today: Iacono: Denarius exec chair; Aris Mining role ended with the 2022 merger (unverified whether he holds other current public boards). CEO Restrepo-Solano: Denarius only verified. Board added two directors June 2026 (Blanco, Al-Ramah).

Fit to this job
Exact fit on paper: Colombian underground narrow-vein gold-silver at small scale with toll/offtake sales is what Gran Colombia did at Segovia, and Iacono's team ran that. Region and permitting (ANLA, Antioquia) known to them. What is NEW: Spain — a nickel-copper restart (Aguablanca) and a polymetallic VMS (Lomero) in a jurisdiction none of them has operated in, funded with JV minority stakes and notes. Execution at Zancudo has been slow despite the fit.
Skin & pay
5/5 — large stake bought with their own money, still buying. Iacono ~80.8M shares / 16.0% (MarketScreener) — includes options exercised for 15M shares (C$8.5M) July 2026 and an open-market buy of 260k shares (C$205k) May 2026; insiders net buyers C$8.7M over 12 months. CFO Davies exercised 249k options Feb 2026. CEO Restrepo-Solano comp US$698k (26% salary) at a ~C$280M market cap — about 0.3%, acceptable. Iacono's own pay not retrieved. Circular not fetched. (https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/DENARIUS-METALS-CORP-111483007/company/ ; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/neoe-dmet/denarius-metals-shares/management)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Pattern of missed timelines: Zancudo plant ~2 years late, Aguablanca restart ~2-3 years late, each slip disclosed as a new target rather than a miss.
  • Three-way founder/affiliate ownership (Iacono 16%, Farringford Foundation 15%, Aris 12%) — related-party dynamics; Aris offtake/toll history.
  • Layered convertibles and notes; equity financed partly by warrant exercises rather than fundamentals.
  • Iacono's history includes the Pacific Rubiales equity wipe-out (unverified this session) alongside real wins.

A "silver" developer whose value is three-quarters manganese — a big, well-drilled, 100%-owned Peruvian deposit with a complex four-product flowsheet and no economic study after six years

Gate Whether a four-product hydromet plant at 4,200 m makes money — and the answer is mostly a manganese-sulphate price, not a silver price. Next catalyst
Berenguela PFS — Q1 2027 (DRA Global)
Partly funded to the next catalyst Funded through the PFS with ~6 months to spare. Not funded for a feasibility study, permitting or any plant; expect a C$15–25M raise in 2027, historically written by Eric Sprott (24%) — the price is set by one holder's appetite (my estimate).
Thesis

Berenguela, at 4,200 m in Puno, is a carbonate-replacement Ag-Cu-Mn-Zn deposit worked from 1906 and optioned by ASARCO, Silver Standard and Valor before Aftermath bought it from SSR Mining (2020; final payment made early, Nov 2025; 100% owned, no remaining payments). The Nov 2025 MRE — 439 holes, open-pit constrained — gives M&I 51.6 Mt @ 74 g/t Ag, 5.7% Mn, 0.63% Cu, 0.33% Zn (122.5 Moz Ag, 2.93 Mt Mn, 717 Mlb Cu), Inferred 14.3 Mt.

The plan is a hydrometallurgical plant: sulphuric/SO2 reductive leach → copper by SX/EW → zinc precipitate → manganese sulphate crystallised to 99.9% HPMSM (battery-grade) → silver by cyanidation of the residue; bench tests show 95% Mn and 89–95% Ag extraction. A PFS with DRA Global / SENET started Feb 2026 and is guided for Q1 2027 — no PEA was done. Cash C$21.8M, no debt, ~C$14M/yr burn; Eric Sprott owns ~24% and wrote the whole Nov 2024 raise.

Phase 3 drilling (90 holes) returned 48.5 m @ 438 g/t Ag / 2.2% Cu / 24.9% Mn and 70 m @ 230 g/t; Phase 4 is testing Copper East and a 2 km skarn anomaly. A US critical-minerals subsidiary with retired USMC generals on its advisory board is chasing DPA / DOE / EXIM money for the HPMSM.

Chile: Challacollo (35 Moz Ag Indicated, permitted DIA, drilling restarted Jul 2026 after the contractor quit) and Cachinal (15 Moz, DIA approved Jul 2026, the 2023 sale never closed).

The Gate

Whether a four-product hydromet plant at 4,200 m makes money — and the answer is mostly a manganese-sulphate price, not a silver price. On the company's own NSR model, manganese is ~75% of value, silver ~13%, copper ~11%. So the PFS (Q1 2027) is really an HPMSM feasibility question: reagent supply (sulphuric acid and SO2 trucked or made on site), acid consumption (never disclosed), plant location and throughput trade-offs, and an offtake market for high-purity manganese sulphate that is thin, China-dominated and price-volatile. Six years after optioning the asset there is no capex, NPV or IRR; SSR's original PFS deadline (Nov 2025) was missed and waived.

Sub-gates
  1. Puno — the most anti-Fujimori region in Peru (86% Sánchez in June), site of the Jan 2023 Juliaca killings and the 2011 "Aymarazo" that cancelled Bear Creek's Santa Ana; a September drill permit was delayed over "incorrect identification of indigenous groups"; consulta previa and water permits are undisclosed.
  2. Funding — C$20M of working capital covers the PFS, not a feasibility study or a plant; another raise in 2027 is near-certain on a stock down ~39% YTD.
  3. Alignment — officers and directors have been steady sellers for a year while Sprott is the only buyer.

If you want silver exposure, this is the wrong vehicle: the silver is a by-product credit on a manganese project. If you want a Western-Hemisphere HPMSM option with 122 Moz of silver attached, it is the only one listed.

Rule screen applies only once the PFS exists — and should be run at a stressed HPMSM price, not a silver price.
Valuation Anchor

Cheapest silver ounces in the file on paper (~US$1.2/oz M&I) and the least meaningful number in it. Price the company as what it is: a pre-study manganese-sulphate project with 122 Moz of silver and 717 Mlb of copper as credits, in Puno, with a plant nobody has costed.

The bull case is a PFS that shows a US$300–500M capex plant making ~US$150–250M/yr of margin across four products at spot, with US government critical-minerals money de-risking the build — at which point a US$165M market cap is a fraction of NPV.

The bear case is a PFS whose economics hinge on an HPMSM price that Chinese oversupply sets, at a capex a C$20M company cannot fund.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — defined tonnes, but no study and the wrong metal for the "cheap defined ounces" test. Silver-price scenarios barely move it; HPMSM price and PFS capex do.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~1.2% (May 2025 deck); Chairman Michael Williams ~2.0M shares / 0.6% is the largest insider. CEO Ralph Rushton's holding is not disclosed in the sources reached; his SEDI activity is all sales. Holdings are mostly options and RSUs plus early (2020-era) placement units. 16.7M options outstanding, 7.6M granted Feb 2026 at C$1.10 — now deeply underwater.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Selling, no buying by officers. Sep 26, 2025: several directors sold ~1.9M shares at C$0.97–1.00 (~C$1.8M, post option exercise); Oct 1, 2025: Rushton sold 646k @ C$0.95; Dec 11, 2025: Parker 200k @ ~C$1.02; Sep 9, 2026: Rushton 167k; Sep 11: Dhillon 27k; Sep 23: Hohol 45k — the September 2026 sales are at the 52-week low. The only insider purchase in the period is Sprott's 9.9M shares at C$0.90 (Dec 23, 2025).
Strategic & prominent
Eric Sprott (2176423 Ontario) ~24% — 83.9M shares; built from 14% (2024) via the entire C$10M Nov 2024 placement (22.2M units @ C$0.45 + warrants) and C$8.9M of the Dec 2025 raise; holds ~11M warrants @ C$0.70. The only 10%+ holder, and effectively the company's financier of last resort. Palisades Goldcorp seeded it at C$0.20 in 2020 (10%); current stake undisclosed, likely diluted below 5%. SSR Mining received US$3M in shares as vendor (2020); current holding undisclosed. No Rule, Gentile, Crescat or Van Eck found.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~6% (Global X/Mirae 2.9%, ALPS 1.5%, Tidal/SILJ 1.4%); Sprott ~24%; insiders ~1%; retail ~66–69%. 350.0M shares (Sep 24, 2026); FD 379.5M.

Read: One man owns a quarter of the company and has bought every time it needed money; the people running it own ~1% and have sold at every price from C$1.00 down to C$0.60. The 'insider-aligned 35%' figure that circulates in promotional coverage is Sprott plus management — read it as Sprott. Related-party fees (~C$1.8M cash + C$2.6M stock in FY26) on a C$14M burn are high for a company with no study.

Jurisdiction risk

National: freshly favourable, thin margin. Keiko Fujimori won the Jun 7, 2026 runoff by 49,641 votes, inaugurated Jul 28; a US$33B mining-investment target, 240 authorisations in 2026, permitting fast-track, 40% of royalties to host communities — analysts call it a 12–24-month window.

Local: the worst in this file after Concordia and Titiribí, for different reasons. Puno voted 86% for Sánchez (the resource-nationalist); Aymara groups at Ilave vowed in June not to recognise a Fujimori win, invoking the Jan 2023 Juliaca killings (18 dead; state of emergency to Sep 2023); the 2011 "Aymarazo" cancelled Bear Creek's Santa Ana project outright. Berenguela is 6 km from Santa Lucía with rail to Matarani and grid power — good infrastructure — and has surface-access agreements and a renewed drilling EIA; but a September authorisation was held up over indigenous-group identification, and consulta previa, water rights and a construction EIA are undisclosed. Chile (Challacollo, Cachinal): DIAs approved, low risk, no funding.

National tailwind, regional headwind: Puno is where Peru's mining conflicts have been settled by force, twice in fifteen years.

Differentiator
  1. The only listed Western-Hemisphere HPMSM project with a silver-copper deposit wrapped around it. 2.93 Mt of manganese in M&I, bench-proven to 99.9% battery-grade sulphate, at a moment when US policy (DPA, DOE, EXIM, DFC) is paying for non-Chinese battery inputs — the advisory board of retired generals and an ambassador is aimed squarely at that.
  2. A large, measured, 100%-owned, royalty-light resource with no payments left — 439 holes, Measured category, open-pit shape, rail and power at the door.
  3. Eric Sprott at ~24%, who funded the company alone in Nov 2024 and took half the Dec 2025 raise — the deepest-pocketed anchor of any junior in either file.
  4. A COO (Danny Keating) who ran Giyani's HPMSM project and a technical director with 22 years at First Quantum — the right résumés for the flowsheet.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (manganese) is why the silver name is misleading and why the economics can't be judged by anyone who follows silver — and Sprott's 24% is both the floor and the reason every future raise is priced by one man's appetite. Same fact, two sides.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, but conversion is done · moves the needle: low–medium. The resource is already Measured + Indicated; Phase 3 (90 holes) produced spectacular silver intercepts (48.5 m @ 438 g/t; 11.4 m @ 1,042 g/t; 4.95 m @ 882 g/t) that improve the model but don't change the category or the metal mix. Phase 4 targets — Copper East (156 m @ 1.12% Cu, 290 g/t Ag previously) and the 2 km SW skarn anomaly — are the genuine upside: a copper-rich extension would rebalance value away from manganese, which is what the equity needs. Chile: 2,000 m at Challacollo, results pending.

More silver ounces add nothing here. More copper would.

Next Catalyst

Berenguela PFS (Q1 2027) — capex, NPV and the HPMSM price assumption; Phase 4 Copper East and SW Intrusive assays (Q4 2026); Challacollo results; any US critical-minerals grant, loan or offtake; a financing (likely 2027, likely Sprott-led); permitting milestones — consulta previa, water.

Open Questions
  • What HPMSM price does the PFS assume, and what does NPV look like at a stressed (Chinese-oversupply) price?
  • Acid and SO₂ consumption and supply at 4,200 m — trucked from where, at what cost per tonne?
  • Is consulta previa complete, and who are the correctly identified indigenous groups?
  • Does the SW skarn or Copper East deliver enough copper to make this a Cu-Ag project with a Mn credit rather than the reverse?
  • Why has the share price fallen 39% in a silver bull market while drilling delivered — is the market saying "not a silver stock" or "no study"?
  • What does Sprott do at the next raise — and what happens to the equity if he doesn't?
Context & updates
PFS progress (Aug 25, 2026)

DRA/SENET: gap analysis complete; trade-off studies on throughput, plant location, reagent supply and infrastructure done with indicative economics (undisclosed); 9-hole geotech programme with Amphos 21 underway; "on schedule and on budget" for early 2027. No PEA.

Ownership consolidated (Dec 29, 2025)

Acquired Sociedad Minera Berenguela S.A. and Fossores Ltd; final US$1.55M to SSR paid Nov 24, 2025 (discounted, a year early); SSR waived the PFS-by-Nov-2025 condition. Royalties: SSR sliding 1.0–1.25% NSR plus a 1% revenue royalty and a reported 2% copper-revenue royalty (VDM) — the stack is inconsistently described; check the Jan 2026 technical report.

Financing (Dec 23, 2025)

C$20.0M LIFE at C$0.90, no warrants, Research Capital / Red Cloud; Sprott took C$8.9M. Post year-end: C$3.2M from 7.1M warrants @ C$0.45. FY26 (May) cash C$21.8M, working capital C$20.5M, debt nil; net loss C$18.8M; auditor going-concern boilerplate.

Aside

The company is chronically called a silver developer by newsletters; its own NSR model says 75% manganese. Note also that the Kaizen/HPX link sometimes attached to Berenguela is wrong — the vendor was SSR Mining, the prior optionee Valor Resources.

A 204 koz gold-antimony deposit with a 17% IRR PEA, 95% of a 2 Moz historic goldfield, and an undrilled target 3 km from OceanaGold's 17 g/t WKP — priced at US$480/oz AuEq, five weeks before an election that could revoke the fast-track it depends on

Gate Whether New Zealand's fast-track survives the 7 November election — and whether a 204 koz, 5.5-year, 17%-IRR deposit is a mine or a resource. The 1News-Verian poll of Sep 23–27 has the left bloc (Labour 28, Greens 16, TOP 6) at 65 seats against 59 for the governing right; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land, and Auld Creek's access adit sits on DOC land. A change of government lands before Rua's panel decision (~Q2 2027). Sub-gates: (1) the economics — NPV US$42M on US$133M of capex at the base deck is a 0.3× project; it only clears the Rule bar at spot gold and a US$27,000/t antimony price that has since halved in China (US$13,300) and is US$19,250 in Europe; mineable shapes in the PEA are 22–27% below the headline ounces and it relies on Inferred; (2) the vein system — 0.6 m at 136 g/t AuEq headlines against a 3.7 g/t Inferred bulk grade: nuggety, narrow, orogenic; the MRE update must convert Inferred to Indicated, not just add ounces; (3) the treasury — C$29.6M at June against a C$17–20M/yr burn and 9,000 m at Glamorgan; the company itself guides C$10–15M by Q2 2027 and 'may need to secure additional financing' — a raise is coming, probably on Glamorgan results or the PFS; (4) the Siren overhang — Siren Gold holds 11.4% in escrow releasing through November and has started selling (700k @ C$1.15, Aug 27); (5) antimony marketing — a separate Sb concentrate to four unnamed metal traders, unproven at scale.
