Thesis

Rua consolidated the Reefton Goldfield (South Island; >2 Moz produced historically at 9–50 g/t) by buying Siren Gold's assets in Nov 2024 for A$20M in shares, taking its ground from 34,000 to ~125,000 ha. The flagship is Auld Creek, a gold-antimony orogenic system 3 km south of Reefton: MRE (Feb 2026) Indicated 54 koz + Inferred 150 koz AuEq at 3.7–5.7 g/t, ~1 km of strike, >500 m deep, open in every direction; and a PEA (Apr 2026): 250 ktpa underground, 5.5 years, ~27 koz AuEq/yr, capex US$133M, AISC US$1,850, after-tax NPV5% US$42M and IRR 17% at US$3,300 Au / US$27,000/t Sb, US$113M and 36% at US$4,700. Antimony (~30% of revenue; a listed critical mineral) is recovered by non-cyanide flotation into a separate concentrate. 2026: 19,600 m drilled at Auld Creek with up to six rigs — 0.6 m @ 82.9 g/t Au + 24.8% Sb (136 g/t AuEq), 2.9 m @ 38.8 AuEq, 32 m @ 2.4 AuEq, first visible gold — 18 holes pending; updated MRE Q4 2026 targeting >300 koz AuEq and a PFS in December; second Reefton deposit (Alexander River / Big River / Supreme, ~340 koz Inferred) into a hub-and-spoke plan Q1 2027. Permitting via the Fast-track Approvals Act: Auld Creek referred by the Minister Jul 29, 2026; substantive application October; decision ~Q2 2027 — OceanaGold's WKP went through in ~112 days. Glamorgan (North Island): 46 km², never drilled, >4 km of Au–As soil anomalies and >40 g/t rock chips, 3 km from WKP (1.46 Moz @ 17.3 g/t); nine pads approved Aug 4; 9,000 m with two rigs from Q4 2026, results Q2 2027.

Cash C$29.6M (Jun 30) after a C$33M raise at C$1.10 in January (no warrants; Franklin Templeton 6%); TSX and NZX listings Feb 2026. CEO Rob Eckford (ex-Aris CFO), chair Oliver Lennox-King (Roxgold, Teranga; 6% holder), COO Simon Henderson (credited with the WKP discovery). Stock C$1.42, +97% in a year; consensus target C$2.37.

The Gate

Whether New Zealand's fast-track survives the 7 November election — and whether a 204 koz, 5.5-year, 17%-IRR deposit is a mine or a resource. The 1News-Verian poll of Sep 23–27 has the left bloc (Labour 28, Greens 16, TOP 6) at 65 seats against 59 for the governing right; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land, and Auld Creek's access adit sits on DOC land. A change of government lands before Rua's panel decision (~Q2 2027).

Sub-gates
  1. The economics — NPV US$42M on US$133M of capex at the base deck is a 0.3× project; it only clears the Rule bar at spot gold and a US$27,000/t antimony price that has since halved in China (US$13,300) and is US$19,250 in Europe; mineable shapes in the PEA are 22–27% below the headline ounces and it relies on Inferred.
  2. The vein system — 0.6 m at 136 g/t AuEq headlines against a 3.7 g/t Inferred bulk grade: nuggety, narrow, orogenic; the MRE update must convert Inferred to Indicated, not just add ounces.
  3. The treasury — C$29.6M at June against a C$17–20M/yr burn and 9,000 m at Glamorgan; the company itself guides C$10–15M by Q2 2027 and 'may need to secure additional financing' — a raise is coming, probably on Glamorgan results or the PFS.
  4. The Siren overhang — Siren Gold holds 11.4% in escrow releasing through November and has started selling (700k @ C$1.15, Aug 27).
  5. Antimony marketing — a separate Sb concentrate to four unnamed metal traders, unproven at scale.

Two gates on one card: an election that could close the permitting door, and a study that says the flagship is marginal without the antimony price it was written at.

District Inferred (Oct 2024, Siren): Alexander River 130 koz @ 4.1 g/t, Big River 70 koz @ 3.3, Supreme 30 koz — ~340 koz including the old Auld Creek figure. 2026 drilling: ACDDH119 0.6 m @ 82.9 g/t Au + 24.8% Sb from 238 m; ACDDH112 2.9 m @ 38.8 AuEq; ACDDH103 7.0 m @ 9.9 AuEq; ACDDH104 32 m @ 2.4 AuEq from 332 m; ACDDH106/108 11.3 m @ 5.7 and 6.1 g/t Au. Satellites: Supreme 0.9 m @ 26.9 g/t; Caledonian 4.0 m @ 6.9 g/t. Glamorgan: no drilling yet — 4,137 soils, Au–As anomalies over >4 km (Sutcliff 1.3 km, Wires Ridge 2.1 km, Tairua 1.6 km), rock chips >40 g/t Au and >200 g/t Ag, CSAMT done.
NPV : capex0.3× at the base deck; ~0.9× at spot — fails the Rule test at base, marginal at spot. IRR 17% fails the 25% bar at base, passes at spot. EV per AuEq ounce: ~US$480 on 204 koz; ~US$290 on the ~340 koz district total — expensive for Inferred-heavy narrow-vein ounces, cheap only if the Q4 MRE lands at >300 koz and Glamorgan hits. Compare Santana (Bendigo-Ophir, 2.34 Moz, PFS NPV A$1.5B, decision Oct 29) for what the market pays a NZ developer with a real study.
Valuation Anchor

~US$480 per AuEq ounce on a 204 koz resource; a PEA whose NPV at spot roughly equals the EV; and an undrilled Glamorgan worth, on the market's arithmetic, nothing. That last point is the case: at C$164M the market pays for Auld Creek plus optimism, and Glamorgan — 3 km from a 1.46 Moz, 17 g/t deposit that OceanaGold just consented, found by the same geologist who is Rua's COO — is the free option.

The re-rate path: Q4 MRE >300 koz with Indicated conversion → PFS with a better base case → fast-track decision Q2 2027 → Glamorgan's first holes (results Q2 2027). Any one of those is 1.5×; Glamorgan hitting WKP-style grade is the multi-bagger, and nothing else on the card is.

The bear case starts on Nov 7: a Labour-Greens government revokes or stalls fast-track, the PFS confirms a 17% IRR, Siren finishes selling, and the company raises at C$0.90 in mid-2027 to drill Glamorgan anyway.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — the Argenta archetype with a study attached: the study says 'marginal', the district says 'maybe'.

Shareholder structure

D&O ~8.0%. Chair Oliver Lennox-King 6.88M shares / ~6% — C$2.3M bought over twelve months incl. C$1M in the Jun 2025 placement and 1.39M shares at C$0.18 in Oct 2024; the largest insider. CEO Rob Eckford 581k shares + 2.2M options; bought 19,000 in Jul 2026. COO Simon Henderson (WKP discovery). 7.66M options at C$0.60–1.43. Interim CFO Darren Prins (Sep 2026, CFO on leave).
Insider activity (12 mo)
Net buyers. Lennox-King's placement participation and open-market buys; Eckford 19k (Jul 2026); insiders took 1.53M shares in the Jun 2025 raise. No insider selling found. The selling is the Siren Gold block: 700k @ C$1.15 on Aug 27 with escrow releases through November.
Strategic & prominent
Siren Gold (ASX) 11.4% — vendor paper, not strategic, and selling. Konwave 7.2%, Franklin Templeton 6.05%, Mackenzie 2.3%, IG 1.0%, ICM and Libra named. Eric Sprott and Peter Marrone are cited as holders by one promotional outlet only — no filing found; treat as unverified and <10%. No OceanaGold, Evolution or other producer; no Rule, McEwen, Palisades or Crescat position found.
Institutions / retail
Company: institutions >40% post-January; filings-based: institutions ~11%, Siren 11–12%, insiders ~8%, retail ~69%. 115.6M shares, FD ~125M; a ~6:1 consolidation in 2024–25. 2,153 registered holders at NZX listing.

Read: A chair who has put C$2.3M of his own money in at prices from C$0.18 to C$1.10 is the strongest insider signal in the small-cap set here, and the CEO is buying, not selling. Against that: the largest holder is a vendor with an escrow calendar, the 'Sprott' name attached to this stock in promotional coverage has no filing behind it, and the company has had to answer for paid promotion once already. Read the register, not the newsletters.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the most mining-friendly New Zealand in a generation — for five more weeks. The coalition's Fast-track Approvals Act 2024 delivered OceanaGold's WKP consent in ~112 days (Dec 2025); the Crown Minerals Amendment Act 2025 changed the regulator's purpose from 'manage' to 'promote' and created Tier-3 gold permits; the Minerals Strategy targets NZ$2–3B of mineral exports by 2035; the Conservation Amendment Bill (in committee) would ease disposal of conservation land. Auld Creek was referred into fast-track on Jul 29, 2026 (stage 1 of 6); substantive application October; ~six-month panel; decision ~Q2 2027. The election is Nov 7. The latest poll has the left bloc ahead 65–59; the Greens have pledged to revoke fast-track approvals and oppose mining on conservation land; NZ First wants ministerial veto powers back. Auld Creek's surface is private farmland and Ngāi Tahu forestry, but the access adit is on DOC land, and a minister has previously declined a mine extension in the nearby Victoria Conservation Park.

Local: Reefton is pro-mining (a gold town whose residents lobbied DOC to keep a mine road open in 2025); no iwi opposition found at Reefton. Glamorgan is the reverse — ~15,000 ha of public conservation land in the Coromandel, Coromandel Watchdog's home ground (they fought WKP for a decade and called the fast-track 'stacked against communities, iwi and environment'); Māori consultation was scheduled for March 2026 with no position published.

Two projects, two licences: Reefton is the easy one and Glamorgan is the hard one — and Glamorgan is where the upside is.

Differentiator
  1. Control of a 2 Moz historic goldfield — >95% of Reefton — with a defined deposit, a PEA, six rigs and a permitting path a major has just proven.
  2. Antimony — ~30% of Auld Creek's revenue from a critical mineral with no Western primary supply, which is either a strategic premium or a marketing problem; the PEA assumes the former.
  3. Glamorgan — the last undrilled epithermal target next to WKP, held by the team that found WKP; nothing else in this file has a discovery target with a 17 g/t neighbour.
  4. A clean structure — 116M shares, no investor warrants in the last two raises, Franklin and Konwave on the register, insiders net buyers, the chair with C$2.3M of his own money in.
  5. Timing — MRE, PFS, fast-track application and first Glamorgan holes all land inside the next six months.

Read it honestly: the flagship's study is the weakest economics in the file, and the differentiator that matters (Glamorgan) has no drill hole in it yet.

Exploration upside

Discovery-driven · moves the needle: very high — it is the thesis. Reefton: 19,600 m in 2026, 18 holes pending, Q4 MRE targeting >300 koz AuEq with Indicated conversion; satellites Supreme, Caledonian, Alexander River, Big River, Murray Creek, Capleston feeding a hub-and-spoke plan from Q1 2027. Glamorgan: 9,000 m, two rigs, from Q4 2026, ~US$5M, results Q2 2027 — the first drill test of >4 km of surface anomalies 3 km from WKP. A WKP-style intercept (tens of g/t over metres) is the only path to a multiple that does not depend on gold.

Glamorgan's start already slipped from Q2 to Q4 2026. The first three holes will say more about this stock than the next three years at Auld Creek.

Next Catalyst

Oct 2026: remaining Auld Creek assays; substantive fast-track application. Q4 2026: first Glamorgan drilling; Siren escrow fully released (Nov). Nov 7: NZ general election. Nov 13: Q3 financials. Nov–Dec: updated MRE (>300 koz target) + PFS. Q1 2027: second Reefton deposit into the plan. Q2 2027: Glamorgan results; fast-track panel decision; project-financing talks and, realistically, an equity raise.

  • If the government changes on Nov 7, what happens to a referred-but-undecided fast-track application — grandfathered, stalled, or revoked?
  • Who are the four antimony offtake groups, and what does a Western Sb concentrate actually fetch versus the China price?
  • When does the company raise, at what price, and does Siren's 11.4% come out first?
  • What is Glamorgan's first-pass drill plan — depth, target, how many holes before a go/no-go?

Bsolid, or unproven but clean (the default)Track record 3/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 2/5 · Skin in the game 3/5low confidence

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
Robert Eckford (CEO & director, since Apr 2024): Ex-CFO of Aris Gold (Caldas Gold) which merged into Aris Mining 2022; company bio says 'co-founder and CFO of Aris Mining' · Oliver Lennox-King (Non-executive Chairman, since 2024): Ex-chair Fronteer Gold (sold to Newmont ~US$2.3B, 2011) and Roxgold (merged into Fortuna ~C$1.1B, 2021); chair Pangea Goldfields, Aurora Uranium · Simon Henderson (COO & director, since 2024): NZ exploration geologist, orogenic/epithermal specialist; local stakeholder relationships · Simon Delander (VP Risk, Stakeholder & Regulatory Affairs, since unverified): Ex-VP at Endura Mining (formerly Federation Mining, Snowy River NZ) — ran its permitting
Track record
  • Lennox-King: two large exits as chairman — Fronteer to Newmont (2011, top of cycle) and Roxgold to Fortuna (2021, mid-cycle); Roxgold actually built and ran Yaramokosource
  • Eckford: finance executive (CFO Aris Gold/Caldas, Marmato Colombia), not a mine builder or discoverer; first CEO role (https://ruagold.com/team/; https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-rua/rua-gold-shares/management)
  • Rua formed 2024 (Reefton Resources + Siren Gold merger, per prior knowledge — unverified); NZX secondary listing Feb 2026; Auld Creek PEA May 2026: after-tax NPV5 US$42M, IRR 17%, capex US$133M, 5.5-yr life, ~27koz AuEq/yr at US$3,300 goldsource
  • Auld Creek accepted into NZ fast-track approvals (Jul 2026); PFS targeted Q4 2026, permits Q2 2027source
  • Director Richard Thomas was COO of Aris Mining; Tyron Breytenbach was SVP Capital Markets at Aris — the board is an Aris alumni groupsource

Boards today: Eckford: 1 (Rua). Lennox-King: Rua chair plus other chairmanships (Pangea Goldfields, Aurora Uranium) — at least 3, exact count unverified. Breytenbach is CEO of Lithium Africa Resources.

Fit to this job
Stage: early explorer with a thin PEA, aiming to become a small gold-antimony producer in New Zealand. The chair's wins came from large discoveries sold to majors, not from building small mines; the CEO is a CFO by trade. Nobody on the executive has built or run a mine in New Zealand; the NZ permitting experience is Delander (Endura/Federation) and Henderson's local network. New for them: everything from PFS to permitting under NZ's fast-track regime, antimony marketing, and a 5.5-year-life project whose economics barely clear a 17% IRR at US$3,300 gold.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Eckford ~0.54% (~C$0.8M); chairman Lennox-King bought ~C$2.3M of shares in the market over the trailing 12 months — the best open-market buying signal in this batch. CEO total comp 2025 C$664k (40% salary, 60% bonus/stock/options) — high for a C$150M explorer. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsx-rua/rua-gold-shares/management. Circular not fetched.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

  • Resource delivered at roughly a quarter of the ounces guided three months earlier
  • CEO comp C$664k at a ~C$150M market cap (0.4% of cap) with 60% in equity awards
  • CEO owns only 0.54% — alignment comes from the chair, not the CEO

Thesis

El Quevar, at 4,800 m in Salta's Puna, was found by Apex Silver (2004), advanced by Hochschild, Golden Minerals (2009–24) and Barrick (earn-in 2020–24, US$6M spent, withdrew) — 414 holes and >US$100M of inflation-adjusted spend — before Argenta (ex-Butte Energy) bought 100% for US$3.5M cash, no royalty to the vendor, in Oct 2024.

What it bought is Yaxtché: 2.93 Mt @ 482 g/t Ag for 45.3 Moz Indicated + 4.1 Moz Inferred — grade among the highest of any undeveloped silver resource, tonnage among the smallest — plus a 100-person camp, a 1,250 m decline, roads, water permits and an approved exploration EIA.

The thesis is that the previous owners explored 3–5% of a 57,000 ha property looking for a bulk-tonnage system, and that a high-grade vein-and-breccia district is what is actually there: the 2025/26 programme (25,500 m since May 2025, upsized three times to 45,000 m for 2026) has extended Yaxtché ~270 m and found Mani-Copan (4,982 g/t over 7.5 m, 500 m south), a Au-Cu system at Carmen (0.57 g/t Au + 0.58% Cu over 44 m), and 20+ untested targets. Sep 2026 metallurgy: 95% average rougher recovery, concentrates to 14,857 g/t.

Cash C$30M at Jun 30 (working capital ~C$24M by Sep), no debt, C$60M raised since inception; Frank Giustra ~7.5–10%, Eduardo Elsztain (IRSA/Cresud) ~9–10%. Red Cloud target C$1.70; stock C$0.455.

The Gate

Proving there is a mine here, not just a vein — and doing it before the money runs out. Yaxtché's 3.2 Mt is a 6-year mine at 1,500 tpd; Golden Minerals' 2018 PEA put the NPV at US$45M, and neither Hochschild, Golden nor Barrick chose to build it. The updated MRE is guided H1 2027 and any economic study ~Q4 2028 — a long runway on ~C$2.3M/month of burn against ~C$24M, which means a financing in 2027 on a stock that has fallen 61% from its February high with C$0.80 LIFE paper and C$0.60 warrants underwater.

Sub-gates
  1. Tonnage — 45,000 m has to turn Mani-Copan and the step-outs into tens of millions of new ounces, not just spectacular metre-intervals.
  2. Concentrate quality — historic concentrates carried As/Sb/Bi penalties and recovery varied by zone; the Sep 2026 tests are encouraging but not locked-cycle.
  3. Altitude and logistics — 4,800 m, 50–200 mm of rain, seasonal access, Puna water.
  4. The sellers — both strategic holders and two directors have been net sellers since Sep 2025 (data-vendor sourced, unverified against SEDI), and nobody inside bought in 2026.

Every prior owner's exit is data. The bull case has to explain why Barrick, with US$6M in and a 70% earn-in, walked in April 2024.

Valuation Anchor

~US$1.5 per Indicated ounce — computable, and the whole debate is whether the denominator is real. If the 2026 programme lifts the resource to 70–100 Moz at similar grade and a 2028 study shows a modest-capex underground mine (the camp, decline and permits already exist), then at US$50+ silver the NPV is plausibly US$500M–1B and today's EV is 10–15% of it — the Red Cloud C$1.70 case.

If tonnage stays near 3–4 Mt, this is a US$100M company with a high-grade vein that three majors declined, waiting for a study in 2028. Unlike Aftermath, the silver-price columns do move this name — it is the purest silver exposure in the developer set.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — Indicated ounces but no study, and the value case rests on discovery, not on what is defined.

Management's own stake is options. Nobody inside bought the 61% drawdown. The register is a 2024–25 vote of confidence and a 2026 vote of patience, at best.

Jurisdiction risk

National: the best it has been in a generation. Milei's coalition won the Oct 2025 midterms; export duties on mining cut to 0% (Aug 2025); Decree 482/2026 restored the 1993 Mining Investment Law's stability certificate and VAT refunds; RIGI has approved ~US$9B including AbraSilver's Diablillos next door (El Quevar itself is likely below the US$200M RIGI threshold and has filed under the 1993 law); capital controls largely lifted; a US$20B US Treasury swap line behind the peso. The Apr 2026 glacier-law reform narrowed protection and handed periglacial oversight to provinces — relevant at 4,500–5,100 m and being litigated.

Provincial / local: strong. Salta is the Fraser Institute's top Latin American jurisdiction (2024), hosts Taca Taca, Rincón and Diablillos, and owns the surface rights (seven easements granted). Kolla community engagement documented and positive; 80% Salta workforce; no conflict found. The real local constraints are physical — altitude, water (permits for 60 m³/day), seasonal access, power 20 km away.

This is the mirror of Aftermath: national and regional politics are the tailwind; geology and the balance sheet are the risk.

Differentiator
  1. Grade — 482 g/t Indicated is exceptional — inside a district almost nobody has explored. Prior owners drilled 3–5% of 57,000 ha chasing bulk tonnage; Argenta is finding high-grade shoots (Mani-Copan) and a separate Au-Cu system (Carmen) with the first systematic surface programme (3,000+ talus samples, 720 km of ground mag).
  2. Infrastructure bought for US$3.5M — camp, decline, roads, water permits, EIA, magazine, gas and HV lines within 20 km — that would cost several times the purchase price to replace.
  3. Two backers with names and cheque-books — Giustra (Fiore) from the listing, Elsztain (IRSA/Cresud, Austral Gold) with a board seat since May 2025 — and a Red Cloud/Raymond James syndicate that has raised C$38M in two bought deals.
  4. Pure silver — no AgEq arithmetic, no by-product deck; it is the cleanest silver-price torque among the developers.

Read it honestly: the differentiator (grade in narrow, high-grade shoots) is why tonnage is small and why the three previous owners, who wanted scale, left. And the two backers have been reducing, not adding, since the stock peaked — the names are a vote from 2024–25, not 2026.

Exploration upside

Discovery-driven · moves the needle: very high — it is the thesis. 45,000 m in 2026 (two rigs; 40% resource expansion, 60% discovery); >25,500 m and 89 holes since May 2025. Yaxtché extended ~270 m; Mani-Copan is a new high-grade zone 500 m south; Carmen a Au-Cu system 350 m NE; Argentina target 1.5 km out; 20+ targets from mag and surface sampling. The next MRE (H1 2027) is the first time the drilling gets counted. Watch the ratio of metre-intervals to ounces — bonanza grades over 1 m add headlines, not tonnes.

Argenta needs tonnes more than grade; every release should be read for width × continuity, not peak g/t.

Next Catalyst

Ongoing 2026 assays (40–70% pending at each release) through Q4; locked-cycle metallurgy and concentrate specs (next 45–60 days from Sep 21); IP/CSAMT geophysics and new target drilling; updated MRE H1 2027; a financing in 2027; environmental baseline (Ausenco) complete; economic study ~Q4 2028.

Open Questions
  • Why did Barrick walk in April 2024 after US$6M and a 70% earn-in — what did they conclude about scale?
  • How many ounces does the 2027 MRE add, and at what tonnage — is this a 50 Moz or a 100 Moz deposit?
  • Do the As/Sb/Bi penalties that hit historic concentrates reappear in locked-cycle tests?
  • Who funds 2027 — Giustra and Elsztain again, or the market at a lower price?
  • What does a 1,500 tpd underground mine at 4,800 m cost to build and run — and has anyone re-run the 2018 PEA at today's silver price?
  • Is Carmen a distraction or a second deposit?

Thesis

A micro-cap sitting on a very large drill database in the Abitibi, trying to re-cut an old underground deposit as an open-pit starter + underground story. Emperor optioned Duquesne West from Globex/Duparquet Assets (Oct 2022), rebuilt the geological model with AI-assisted targeting, and more than doubled the historical 727 koz to 1.46 Moz.

The 2025/26 programme (66 holes, 20,479 m, on budget) plus 7,884 m of resampled historical core is meant to (a) thicken the pit-shell lenses near surface and (b) convert Inferred to Indicated ahead of an updated 43-101 and a PEA.

Second leg: Lac Pelletier, 4 km from Rouyn-Noranda, contiguous with Agnico Eagle's Wasamac (2.2 Moz M&I) on the same shear — acquired for assumed closure liabilities (~C$305k in bonds) plus a purchase from Maritime; it carries a granted 1,000 tpd underground extraction permit. CEO John Florek (P.Geol); C$11.1M LIFE raise Oct 2025 (oversubscribed) funded the season.

The Gate

Turning a 100%-Inferred, historically-underground deposit into a bankable open-pit case — does the near-surface envelope carry enough grade at a workable strip ratio once properly modelled? Free/visible gold and bonanza intervals make the grade nuggety; APEX had to use ordinary kriging with locally-varying anisotropy to get continuity, and nothing is yet Indicated.

Sub-gates
  1. The option isn't done — C$10M cash + 15M shares + C$12M exploration over five years to Duparquet Assets (50% Globex); year-3 paid Jan 2026, year-4 due Jan 2027.
  2. Treasury — the Oct 2025 C$11.1M has largely been spent on the season, so a PEA and the 2027 option payment almost certainly mean another raise on a ~C$65–95M cap.
  3. Disclosure hygiene — an Oct 2025 release mis-stated the resource grade as 5.42 g/t and needed a same-day correction, the company moved to semi-annual reporting in Jun 2026, and assay turnaround has slipped twice on lab backlogs.

Lac Pelletier's closure-plan approval was guided end-June → now "before end of Q3" — watch for a third slip.

Lac Pelletier (historical, non-compliant): 89.4 koz M&I @ 4.08 g/t + 137.6 koz Inf @ 3.89 g/t; 3.3 km of underground development with a portal, 105,000 m drilled, 1% NSR to Metalla.

Valuation Anchor

~US$40/oz on Inferred ounces (US$60M ÷ 1.46 Moz; ~US$35–50/oz across the mcap range). Cheap-looking against Abitibi peers with Indicated resources, but the Inferred discount is deserved: nothing here can go into a reserve yet.

The honest anchor is EV per future Indicated ounce — if half converts, you are paying ~US$80/oz for the credible part, which is fair rather than cheap.

Dilution overhang is structural: 15M option shares + C$10M of option cash + a PEA to fund. Lac Pelletier is carried at roughly nothing and is the free option.

Bucket call: grade / discovery / optionality, not "cheap defined ounces", because the ounces aren't defined to the standard the cheap bucket requires.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~5.8–6.6% (board "collectively 5.8%", Sep 2026 deck; insiders 6.55% per Streetwise). Per person: Nigel Horsley (VP, founder) ~4.8M / 2.5%; John Florek (CEO) ~3.1M / 1.6%; John Williamson (Chair) ~2.4M / 1.2%; Sean Mager (CFO) ~1.7M; Ian Harris ~1.0M. Mostly bought — placements and market — on top of 17.4M options outstanding.
Insider activity (12 mo)
Buying. Florek bought ~253,500 shares in the market at C$0.165–0.175 (Dec 29, 2025 – Jan 3, 2026, ~C$44k); further un-named insider buys Jan and Mar 2026. Horsley exercised and sold 500k options (Dec 31, 2025). Net: small cash buying by the CEO at the lows.
Strategic & prominent
Robert McEwen (Evanachan) ~7% — largest holder, all cash: 8M units @ C$0.125 (Mar 2024), 5M @ C$0.15 (Mar 2025, half that raise), 750k @ C$0.20 (Oct 2025). Rick Rule — "invested in 2025" per company deck, size undisclosed (presumably the Oct 2025 LIFE). Maritime Resources received 12.5M shares (10.8%) for Lac Pelletier (Mar 2025) and sold the whole block in Nov 2025 at ~C$0.16 — a vendor exit, not a vote.
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~7%, insiders ~6.5%, retail ~86%. No 10%+ holder, no control block. 196.1M shares; 28.8M warrants + 17.4M options → FD 242.3M.

Read: The two names that matter here both put cash in at the bottom: McEwen has averaged up across three placements and Rule chose it in 2025. Management's ~6% is real money on a ~C$65M cap but small in absolute terms. The retail-heavy register is why the stock moves 10%+ on a drill hole — and why a financing will be priced to whoever shows up.

Jurisdiction risk

National / provincial: as good as it gets. Québec, Abitibi — road, hydro, Rouyn-Noranda labour, labs at Val d'Or, a permitting regime the whole industry knows.

Local: low. Duquesne West is 10 km from Duparquet in the historic camp; Lac Pelletier sits inside Rouyn-Noranda city limits, but as a past-producing mine site with an existing extraction permit and closure plan, not a greenfield fight. No organised opposition known.

Jurisdiction is not the discount here — geology and balance sheet are.

Differentiator
  1. Data density per dollar of market cap. ~143,000 m of drilling (much of it inherited) on a ~US$60M company is unusual — most peers at this cap have a fraction of that, so the resource-growth story is about re-modelling and infill, not blind step-outs.
  2. High-grade shoots inside a bulk envelope — 61.5 g/t over 15 m and 369.6 g/t over 2.4 m are real, and free gold was not previously recognised or targeted, which is optionality a 1.69 g/t average understates.
  3. A permitted second asset — Lac Pelletier's 1,000 tpd extraction permit, existing portal and underground development, on Agnico's Wasamac shear, is a rare thing for a micro-cap to own (subject to the liability transfer closing).

Read it honestly: the bonanza lenses are the differentiator and the reason the resource is hard to model and still all Inferred — the same fact seen from two sides. And "AI-driven exploration" is marketing until the Indicated tonnes show up.

Exploration upside

Drill-confirmed, better tonnes near surface · moves the needle: high. 21.3 m @ 3.0 g/t from 64 m (DQ26-43) and 24.1 m @ 2.6 g/t from 45 m incl. 7.1 m @ 7.5 g/t (DQ26-52) sit ~400 m apart — that continuity is the starter-pit argument. Deep bonanza shoots (15 m @ 61.5 g/t at ~400 m; 20.1 m @ 5.0 g/t; 35.9 m @ 3.1 g/t) are underground material, not pit material. 107.7 m @ 0.5 g/t is the bulk-envelope argument. Only ~45% of the season's assays (incl. historical core) reported as of Sep 9 — the rest lands through Q4.

Here exploration is not a bonus: conversion to Indicated and the pit-shell grade are the thesis.

Next Catalyst

Sep 29 release: DQ26-37 32.0 m @ 5.9 g/t incl. 2.6 m @ 22.4 g/t (infill, inside the resource, 59% assayed); DQ26-46 20.1 m @ 5.0 g/t; step-out DQ26-47 14.7 m @ 0.5 g/t. 44 of 66 holes reported; ~50% of assays incl. 7,884 m of historical resampling pending; drilling resumes late October; MRE and PEA 'to follow' — undated. Remaining ~55% of 2025/26 assays incl. historical core (Q4 2026); MRNF approval of the Lac Pelletier closure plan and liability transfer from Eldorado (guided Q3 2026 — check); updated Lac Pelletier 43-101 (commenced Jul 2026); updated Duquesne West MRE → PEA (no date); year-4 option payment (Jan 2027); a financing.

Open Questions
  • What does the pit-constrained portion grade on its own, and at what strip?
  • How much of the 1.46 Moz converts to Indicated in the updated MRE — and when is that MRE actually dated?
  • Does Emperor exercise the Globex option outright, renegotiate, or dilute to do it?
  • Does the Lac Pelletier liability transfer close with Eldorado and MRNF, and what does the updated 43-101 say about the historical ounces?
  • Is Agnico (Wasamac) a natural buyer of Lac Pelletier — or of the whole company?

Effect on the odds: none — neutral by default; odds move only with evidence.

People
John Florek (President & CEO, director, since Nov 2022): M.Sc., P.Geo; ex-Superintendent of Geology Detour Lake (Kirkland Lake Gold), senior geologist Barrick Hemlo, Placer Dome; director McEwen Inc. · John Williamson (Chairman (independent), since unverified): Founder of Metals Group; says he has founded 20+ companies and raised C$1B+ · John Labrecque (VP Exploration, since ~2025): 26 yrs; Hemlo 'Developer of the Year' 2008 · Sean Mager (CFO & director, since ~2020): Co-founder Metals Group
Track record
  • Florek: a mine geologist (Detour, Hemlo) in his first CEO role; no prior company run or sold foundsource
  • Williamson/Metals Group: claims 20+ companies founded — individual outcomes not verifiable from company material; the pattern (many small shells) is the risk to checksource
  • Under Florek: maiden MRE at Duquesne West Jul 2025, 1.46Moz at 1.69 g/t (doubling the 727koz historical); acquired Lac Pelletier 2025; C$11M LIFE financing Oct 2025; 10–15km drill program 2025–26 with strong hits incl. 15m at 61.5 g/t (Jun 2026) (https://www.gbreports.com/contents/john-florek-2/; https://www.newsfilecorp.com/company/8461/Emperor-Metals-Inc.)
  • Duquesne West is held under option from Duparquet Assets (50% Globex); third-year renewal Jan 2026 cost C$1.0M cash + 3.26M shares (C$600k) — the company does not own its flagshipsource

Boards today: Florek: 2 (Emperor CEO, McEwen Inc. director). Williamson: multiple Metals Group companies — count unverified.

Fit to this job
Explorer stage, Abitibi gold — the CEO and VP Exploration are Abitibi/Ontario mine geologists (Detour, Hemlo), which is the right fit for resource growth and open-pit conceptual work. Nobody on the executive has run a public company to an exit, completed a PEA, or built a mine. New for them: converting the resource into a PEA (talked about for 2026, not yet delivered) and securing the optioned ground.
Skin & pay
2/5 — small stake from grants or cheap founder paper; little buying. Florek ~1.58% (~US$1.2M); insider buying/selling not found. CEO total comp ~US$206k (64% salary) — modest and proportionate to a ~US$77M market cap. Source: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/materials/otc-emau.f/emperor-metals/management. No circular fetched.

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Flagship is optioned, not owned; annual payments of C$1M+ cash plus shares
  • Chairman is a serial company founder (20+) with no verifiable exit record in company material
  • Moved to semi-annual financial reporting in 2026
  • No PEA despite 2025 talk of one 'potentially' in 2026
  • Financials: investor promotion is the largest expense line (C$0.55M in H1 FY25); overhead C$0.7M vs C$0.5M into the ground in H1 FY26; statements not on the company site, several periods missing.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash fell to C$0.25M in January 2025 and was C$1.0M at 31 July 2025; a C$11M LIFE offering in October 2025 left working capital of about C$5.4M by September 2026.
  2. Overhead dominates: in H1 FY26 G&A was C$0.7M against C$0.5M of capitalised exploration, and investor promotion is the single biggest expense line.
  3. Half-year burn was about C$1.3M in H1 FY26, but the 20,479 m 2026 drill program means the current burn is materially higher than filed periods show.
  4. Shares outstanding grew from 103.5M in July 2024 to 196.1M in September 2026, up 89%; the Lac Pelletier purchase was paid largely in shares and the LIFE deal added 44M.
  5. Recurring flow-through financings produce non-cash gains that flatter the reported loss; no debt or streams, only small leases.

Thesis

Freegold Mountain is a large, road-accessible land package (~200 km² along 30 km of the Big Creek Fault, km 82 of the government-maintained Freegold Road, 70 km from Carmacks) that Northern Freegold / Triumph has held since 2006, with more than C$40M of historical work and a Feb 2020 resource of 791 koz Au Indicated (1.0 Moz AuEq) + 707 koz Au Inferred (1.09 Moz AuEq) across Nucleus (oxide-capped, 0.65 g/t), Revenue (Cu-Au-Mo porphyry, 0.38 g/t) and Tinta Hill (Ag-rich veins). Goldcorp took 19.9% in 2017; a Zijin-linked fund took 9.8% in 2018; a 2013 PEA (superseded) showed an after-tax NPV of C$358M at US$1,455 gold on US$500M of capex. Then nothing: the last drill hole was in 2021 (6,615 m; best N21-02 46 m @ 0.54 g/t oxide), the company hit C$2,252 of cash in September 2024 with C$364k owed to management, did a 1-for-10 consolidation (Dec 2022), and has since raised C$9.3M in three non-brokered unit placements (C$0.20, C$0.30, C$0.50) to reach C$5.2M cash at Jun 30, 2026. 2025 exploration spend: C$253k (mapping; the 'Proton Zone' vein showing). 2026 H1: C$124k. Meanwhile it bought a silver property in Utah (Coyote Knoll: US$150k + 4M shares + US$3M in year four), plans an IP survey in BC, and floated a spin-out. Executive Chairman and 'interim' CEO John Anderson since 2019; no analyst coverage; no news release since June 12.

Valuation Anchor

~US$17/oz AuEq — the lowest number in the file, and the least informative. Cheapness per ounce is only a signal when something is being done to convert or grow the ounces; here the last five years of spending went to overhead, promotion, a Utah silver property and a BC geophysics plan.

The bull case is purely arithmetic: a 2 Moz AuEq resource in the Yukon, road-accessible, with a Goldcorp/Newmont and Zijin pedigree, re-studied at US$4,000 gold, is worth many multiples of US$35M — and Western Copper's Casino project next door is why the road exists at all.

The bear case is the company as it actually operates: three placements in eighteen months to fund G&A, a warrant overhang of 34.8M, and a flagship that gets mapping while cash gets spent.

Bucket: grade / discovery / optionality — optionality is the operative word, on someone else eventually doing what this company has not.

Shareholder structure
Management & board
~6.9% per filings-based aggregators (the company says '~37% management, board and key shareholders' — the gap is unexplained and the higher figure has no early-warning support). Executive Chairman / interim CEO John Anderson ~4.8M shares / ~6.6–8% — built through placements (3.5M units in the Jan 2023 raise pre-consolidation, 250k units Nov 2025, 500k units Jun 2026) plus options; the one insider consistently writing cheques. Other directors and officers hold 10k–136k each. 6.9M options at C$0.27–0.58, 4.75M of them granted May 2025 with immediate vesting.
Insider activity (12 mo)
The CEO buys placements; everyone else sells. Anderson: 250k units @ C$0.30 (Nov 2025), 500k @ C$0.50 (Jun 2026). Corporate secretary Moroney sold ~104k shares at C$0.68–0.84 (Feb–Jun 2026); new director Cowley sold 50k at C$0.46–0.61 (Apr–May 2026) — two months after joining the board. One small buy by Schreiner (10k, Sep 23, 2026). Net insider selling ~C$74k in the recent three-month window on a C$48M company.
Strategic & prominent
None current. Goldcorp's 19.9% (2017) became Newmont's and was diluted to 3.45% by 2023 and below the reporting threshold since; the Zijin-linked fund's 9.8% (2018) has vanished from every holder list; Palisades' 9.5% (2021) is sub-2%. Konwave (Gold 2000) ~2.6% is the only institution. The Michael Gentile '~8%' in newsletter coverage is unfiled. No Sprott, Rule or Crescat. Related-party: director Paul Cowley's company billed C$143k in H1 2026 (consulting + share-issuance costs).
Institutions / retail
Institutions ~2.7%, insiders ~7%, retail ~90%. 72.5M shares; FD 114.3M — 34.8M warrants (C$0.175–0.55, to 2027–29) and 6.9M options; the Jun 2026 placement's 10.8M shares come free Oct 13, 2026. 1-for-10 consolidation Dec 2022. No lead broker on any raise since 2023; finders' fees and finder warrants on each.

Read: The strategic register that made this name interesting in 2017–2020 — Goldcorp, a Zijin fund, Palisades — has been diluted out of existence, and no one with a name has replaced them. What remains is a CEO who funds his own placements, a retail float, a warrant overhang equal to half the shares, and officers selling small amounts into every rally. The company's own ownership claims do not reconcile with the filings; treat the filings as the truth.

Jurisdiction risk

National / territorial: tier-one on paper, degraded in practice since Eagle. The Yukon Party won a majority in Nov 2025 on faster permitting, legislated timelines and a new minerals act — but the act is targeted for 2028, and the Eagle Gold heap-leach failure (Jun 2024; cleanup C$377M by Sep 2026; 50+ review-board recommendations, 27 still due by spring 2027) produced a territorial halt on licensing new heap-leach facilities and a rewrite of mine-waste guidelines — directly relevant to a Nucleus oxide heap-leach concept. The Yukon Geological Survey itself says Eagle "negatively impacted investors choosing to risk capital on early-stage projects in the Yukon."

Local: unaddressed. Freegold sits in Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation traditional territory; the company discloses no exploration or cooperation agreement with LSCFN (engagement is a citizen-owned environmental contractor and a 2021 office hire); LSCFN declared a mining moratorium around Claire Lake in Apr 2026 (location relative to Freegold not established) and its chief has criticised the minerals-legislation process. The Freegold Road upgrade beyond km 82 — the company's stated infrastructure advantage — was de-funded in Mar 2025 when the Gateway money moved to the Dempster; it now depends on Casino's YESAB timeline.

Yukon is the reason a 0.58 g/t resource can be called 'tier-one'; post-Eagle Yukon is the reason its likely mining method is on hold.

Differentiator
  1. Two million AuEq ounces on a government road for US$35M — with a Casino-scale neighbour that will bring infrastructure whether Triumph does anything or not.
  2. The land package — 200 km² along 30 km of a productive structure with 20+ zones, WAu breccia and Blue Sky intercepts that were never followed up; if the Dawson Range gets re-rated by Casino's build, this is one of the largest positions in it.
  3. A clean-ish balance sheet for once — C$5.2M cash, no debt, management debts repaid.
  4. The historical validation — Goldcorp at 19.9%, a Zijin fund at 9.8%, Rio Tinto once optioning the BC ground — which says the geology was worth a major's money in 2017–19, even if none of them stayed.

Read it honestly: every differentiator is something that happened to the company, not something it did — the road, the neighbour, the 2017 placement. The only thing it controls, exploration, is the thing it has not done.

Exploration upside

Nothing drilled since 2021 · moves the needle: potentially very high, currently zero. The 2026 plan is mapping and sampling with 'first-pass drill planning' — no metres, no budget. Targets that would matter if tested: WAu breccia at depth, Blue Sky, Revenue's underground high-grade block, the Nucleus oxide cap for a heap-leach case (now regulatorily fraught), and the 2025 Proton Zone showing. A December 2025 newsletter floated RC drilling of Nucleus oxides and re-assaying WAu for tungsten (~15 Mlb W, non-43-101); nothing has been reported. Andalusite Peak (BC) gets an 11.8 line-km IP survey; Coyote Knoll (Utah) a 26-hole permit — the money is going away from the flagship.

The next drill hole at Freegold will be the first in five years. Until it exists, exploration upside is a slide, not a programme.

Next Catalyst

Any drill programme at Freegold (undated, unbudgeted); the June placement's hold expiry (Oct 13, 2026) — 10.8M shares free to trade; Yukon heap-leach guideline rewrite (spring 2027); Casino (Western Copper) permitting progress as a district read-through; Coyote Knoll drilling H2 2026; a possible spin-out; the next placement.

Open Questions
  • Why has a company holding 2 Moz AuEq not drilled it since 2021 — and what, specifically, is the 2026 budget for Freegold versus Utah, BC and G&A?
  • Who actually owns the stock — is the '37% management, board and key shareholders' claim reconcilable with the 6.9% insiders and 2.7% institutions that filings show?
  • What does Nucleus look like as a heap-leach project under the post-Eagle Yukon rules, and is there a non-heap-leach case?
  • Is there any agreement, or any conversation, with Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation?
  • What happens to the share price when 10.8M June-placement shares and 34.8M warrants meet a stock that trades 20–250k shares a day?
  • Is the asset worth more to Western Copper, or to anyone building in the Dawson Range, than to its current owner?

No news release since Jun 12, 2026. The '~8% Michael Gentile' holding cited in Dec 2025 newsletter coverage has no early-warning filing behind it and is treated here as unverified. The 2013 PEA is sometimes quoted at 'C$650M NPV' (pre-tax) — the after-tax figure was C$358M.

Management review
Creal weaknesses: slipped dates, thin fit or thin candourTrack record 2/5 · Fit 2/5 · Candour 3/5 · Skin in the game 3/5

Fifteen years on one property under an interim CEO, serial small placements and no stage advance: a pattern of capital consumed without progress.

Effect on the odds: chance it works 25% → 20%, odds of a 3× 7% → 6%.

People
John Anderson (Executive Chairman & Interim CEO, since Chairman since 2011 (on board since ~2009); interim CEO since Sept/Oct 2019): Age 62. Capital-markets background (Bema Gold IR, Manulife corp dev); founded Deep 6 PLC, American Eagle Oil & Gas, Aquastone Capital gold fund. Has been 'interim' CEO for ~7 years. · Jesse Halle, P.Geo. (VP Exploration, since unverified (quoted as VP Exploration since at least 2021)): Managing director of Halle Geological Services (contractor); porphyry Cu-Au work at Casino, Copper Mountain. Wife Emily Halle is project manager from the same firm. · Rakesh Patel (CFO, since Sept 2017): Part-time; audit partner at DMCL. · Marty Henning, P.Geo. (Principal Geologist, since unverified): 10 years at New Afton block cave.
Track record
  • Anderson: capital-markets/IR career; the companies he founded (Deep 6 PLC, American Eagle Oil & Gas) have no verifiable mine-building or sale outcome foundsource
  • Triumph/Freegold Mountain: ~2 Moz AuEq resource at Revenue-Nucleus already cited in 2020; same resource still the pitch in 2025 — no study, no resource growth found in 6 years (https://investingnews.com/ceo-interviews/triumph-gold-president-director-tony-barresi-freegold-mountain-update-dawson-range-yukon/ ; https://www.stocktitan.net/news/TIGCF/triumph-gold-updates-shareholders-on-operations-engages-market-maker-vfbsh4otjr8u.html)
  • Former president Tony Barresi said in March 2020 the company was 'positioning ourselves as a takeout target'; no takeout happened, Barresi gone, Anderson interim CEO since 2019source
  • Serial small financings: $1.94M at $0.30 (Nov 2025), $3.75M raise (earlier), market maker hired at $6,500/month (May 2025) (https://investingnews.com/triumph-gold-closes-1-93-million-private-placement/ ; https://resourceworld.com/triumph-gold-raising-3-75-million-for-yukon-project/)
  • Board average tenure 12.5 years; Strub and Anderson on board since 2011; Sparks since 2017; only one new director (Cowley, June 2025)source

Boards today: Anderson: Triumph (exec chair + interim CEO); other current public boards not verified. Director Paul Cowley is CEO of two other juniors (Phenom Resources, Indigo Exploration). Director Marco Strub sits on several other juniors (Canada Zinc Metals etc.).

Fit to this job
Team is a capital-markets chairman plus contract geologists. Explorer-stage fit is adequate for a porphyry/epithermal Yukon target (Halle, Henning have porphyry Cu-Au experience). Nobody on the executive has taken a project through PEA/PFS or built anything. Company has been exploring the same property since the Northern Freegold days (2000s) without advancing stage — the 'job' here is simply finding something new, and 15+ years of trying has not produced it.
Skin & pay
3/5 — meaningful stake, mostly founder stock or grants; not selling. Anderson holds ~4.87M shares (~8.0% per MarketScreener; SimplyWall.st says 6.6%), built partly through placements (250k units Nov 2025 = C$75k). Other directors hold <0.3% each. SimplyWall.st flags 'significant insider selling' of ~C$63-74k in the last 3 months (names not verified). CEO comp C$313k, 100% salary (SimplyWall.st) — ~0.65% of a C$48M market cap; modest in absolute terms. Circular not fetched; figures are third-party aggregations. (https://simplywall.st/stocks/ca/materials/tsxv-tig/triumph-gold-shares/management ; https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/TRIUMPH-GOLD-CORP-49477449/company/)

Skin in the game is a signal of the team's own conviction: it never moves the odds, but breaks near-ties in list B of the rankings.

Red flags
  • Interim CEO for ~7 years; no permanent operator hired.
  • Same ~2 Moz AuEq resource marketed for 6+ years with no study or growth — stage never advanced.
  • Immediate-vesting option grants (4.75M at $0.27, May 2025) at a ~C$48M company.
  • Strategy drift: Yukon gold explorer announcing it is 'evaluating silver project acquisitions'.
  • Board refreshment: only one new director in 3 years; average tenure 12.5 years.

Simplified from the original filings (last 8 quarters and 3 fiscal years, C$ millions, fiscal year ends 31 Dec). Every column links to the statements it came from.

What the numbers say
  1. Cash went from near zero to C$5.21M at 30 June 2026 after three placements; at the H1 2026 burn of C$0.73M a quarter that is about 7 quarters.
  2. That burn contains almost no drilling: the permitted 26-hole Coyote Knoll program and the Andalusite Peak IP survey are not yet in the numbers.
  3. Overhead dominates: FY2025 G&A was C$1.49M against C$0.67M spent in the ground, so about two-thirds of cash went to overhead, led by corporate communications.
  4. Shares outstanding rose from 42.8M in December 2024 to 72.1M in June 2026, up 69%, after C$9.3M of unit placements; 34.8M warrants remain.
  5. No debt, but share-based pay was C$1.31M in FY2025, related-party payables exceeded cash for most of 2024–2025, and the statements carry a going-concern note.

Amounts in C$ millions. Because Triumph's figures are very small (statements are in whole dollars, most quarters < C$1M), values are given to TWO decimals rather than one so that the spend chart is not all zeros. Exploration here is mostly EXPENSED (exploration expenditures + property investigation in the income statement); only property acquisition costs and the exploration deposit are capitalised (cf.exp_cap). spend.overhead = operating cash outflow not explained by expensed exploration (i.e. cash G&A incl. working-capital moves); spend.ground = expensed exploration + capitalised acquisition/deposit cash.

How to read a card. The bucket colour on the left is the archetype. The gate is the single thing that has to go right; the differentiator is what the company has that peers don't. When those two are the same fact seen from two sides, that's usually the most honest thing to know about the name.

Reminder on cross-company comparisons: NPV/capex figures sit on each project's own metal-price deck and discount rate, and AuEq/AgEq use different price assumptions per company — read the anchors as shapes, not decimal-precise rankings. Market caps for CSE/TSXV names move 10–30% on single releases; verify live before anchoring. This is research shorthand, not investment advice.
